This playbook should be updated annually or whenever changes are made to the runtime (kernel selection, batching model) or the promotion scoring formula. For questions or exceptions, contact the playbook owner (Maya Chen) or SRE lead (Alejandro Ruiz).

Title: Heterogeneous Workload Shadow Orchestration and Telemetry Spec

Heterogeneous Workload Shadow Orchestration and Telemetry Spec

Overview

Purpose: This document defines a standardized orchestration and telemetry specification for running 'shadow' evaluations across heterogeneous customer workloads (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, multi-turn stateful flows) and across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce actionable, production-realistic signal for model promotion, quantization impact, and regression triage while preserving privacy and minimizing production risk.

Scope: eval harness components, sampling strategies, fingerprinting and workload signatures, capacity-aware routing, telemetry schema, data retention, onboarding steps, and remediation/fast-fail playbook. This is intended for ML Engineers, SREs, and Product owners responsible for model promotion and quality guardrails.

High-level principles

- Non-disruptive: Shadow traffic must not add user-visible latency or affect customer SLOs.
- Representative: Sampling must preserve distributional properties of the target workload (intent mix, sequence length, token distribution).
- Traceable: Every shadow request is tagged with identifiers that tie back to deployment configuration, quant profile, and sampling provenance.
- Cost-aware: Orchestrator must throttle shadow replication under capacity pressure.
- Privacy-first: Use local PII filtering and differential-privacy sampling when required by customer configuration.

Architecture and components

1) Mirroring Proxy (mirrord)
- Deployed as an ingress-layer sidecar or region-edge service.
- Responsible for duplicating production requests to a shadow queue without affecting production response path.
- Tags traffic with: workload_fingerprint, sample_bucket_id, region, model_variant, quant_profile.

2) Shadow Sampler (sampler-service)
- Implements sampling policies (fixed-rate, stratified, capacity-aware, slot-based).
- Maintains per-workload counters and safety budgets.
- Supports on-the-fly rate adjustments via the Control Plane.

3) Replay Store (replay-blob / kafka topics)
- Short-term durable store for shadow payloads (30–90 days depending on retention policy).
- Indexes by fingerprint and sample_bucket.

4) Eval Runner (evald)
- Pulls from Replay Store, executes against target model variant(s) and quant profiles, produces evaluation artifacts.
- Runs both lightweight (latency/throughput) and fidelity evals (semantic-similarity, task-specific metrics).

5) Telemetry Collector (telemetry ingestion layer)
- Central schema-enforced collector that receives delta metrics, logs, and artifacts.
- Emits normalized events to observability pipeline and to the eval dashboard.

6) Audit & Triage UI (eval-console)
- Surface diffs between baseline and candidate variants, grouped by fingerprint slice and quant-profile.
- Provides explainability overlays and links to raw artifacts.

Workload fingerprinting (why and how)

- Fingerprinting objective: group similar requests so shadow sampling preserves within-slice distributions and we can prioritize critical slices.
- Fingerprint components: route_id, intent_hash (top-level classification of user intent), token_length_bucket, device_context (web/mobile/api), language, privacy_flag.
- Implementation: deterministic hash of normalized request headers + canonicalized prompt text (PII redacted).

Sampling strategies

1) Capacity-Aware Stratified Sampling (default)
- Stratify by fingerprint slice (intent + length bucket + language).
- Allocate sampling budget proportional to slice-contribution to production traffic, with minimum floor to ensure coverage of low-frequency critical slices.
- Backpressure: when GPU pools approach 85% utilization, reduce non-critical slice replication by multiplicative decrease.

2) Focused Safety Sampling
- For newly onboarded prompt sets or after model changes, temporarily boost sampling for slices tagged as safety-sensitive by product owners.

3) Weighted Reservoir for Long-Tail
- Maintain a small reservoir of long-tail examples sampled uniformly across customers; useful for regression discovery.

4) Differential Privacy-Constrained Sampling
- Optionally enabled per-customer: samples are drawn in a way that enforces local epsilon budgets; shadow artifacts are tagged and processed under private lanes.

Telemetry schema (key events and fields)

All telemetry events use the eval_event schema v2. Fields below are top-level strings or simple numeric values; evaluators must surface them in dashboards.

- event_type: "shadow_request" | "eval_result" | "model_diff" | "resource_pressure"
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- request_id: unique id (matches production request)
- workload_fingerprint: string
- sample_bucket_id: string
- route_id: string
- model_variant: string (e.g. redwood-phi-3b-v2)
- quant_profile: string (e.g. q4_0_dynamic)
- deployment_mode: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end execution on shadow path)
- tokens_consumed: integer
- similarity_score: float (-1..1) // semantic similarity to baseline output if applicable
- fidelity_delta: float // positive means candidate improved against baseline on chosen metric
- failure_code: string | null
- privacy_flag: true|false
- capacity_flag: OK | THROTTLED | DROPPED

(Example JSON event)
{
  "event_type": "eval_result",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-22T14:33:12Z",
  "request_id": "r-7f3c2a",
  "workload_fingerprint": "intent=translate;len=short;lang=es",
  "model_variant": "redwood-phi-3b-v2",
  "quant_profile": "q4_0_dynamic",
  "latency_ms": 42,
  "tokens_consumed": 34,
  "similarity_score": 0.92,
  "fidelity_delta": -0.03
}

Acceptance criteria and thresholds

- Latency: shadow RTT should not add > 0.5ms to production P50 or cause more than 0.1% of production requests to breach P99 latency.
- Fidelity regression: for any critical slice, fidelity_delta must be >= -0.02 averaged across a 24h window, otherwise fail promotion.
- Embeddings drift: cosine similarity mean should not drop by > 0.015 on embedding baselines for core slices.
- Reranker NDCG: candidate should not degrade NDCG@10 by more than 0.01 for top-customer slices.

Config table (example)

- job_id: string (eval-job-2025-11-02-01)
- target_variants: [baseline, candidate] (as comma-separated string)
- slices: comma-separated list of fingerprint slices
- sampling_policy: capacity_aware|focused_safety|reservoir
- retention_days: numeric (30|90)
- max_parallel_jobs: numeric
- min_samples_per_slice: numeric

Example eval job YAML (for evalctl)

eval_job: eval-job-hetero-2025-11-02
target_variants: baseline=candidate: redwood-phi-3b-v1, candidate: redwood-phi-3b-v2
slices: intent:translate:len:short, intent:qa:len:medium
sampling_policy: capacity_aware
retention_days: 30
min_samples_per_slice: 100

CLI example

# create a shadow eval job from a sample policy
evalctl create --job eval-job-hetero-2025-11-02 --policy capacity_aware --slices "translate:short,qa:medium" --variants "baseline=redwood-phi-3b-v1,candidate=redwood-phi-3b-v2"

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

1) Workload annotation (owner: product/solutions)
- Define critical slices and expected behaviors. Tag prompts that are safety or compliance sensitive.
2) Fingerprint validation (owner: ML infra)
- Run offline fingerprint sampler on representative logs to ensure slice coverage and avoid over-fragmentation.
3) Sampling policy selection (owner: ML Engineer)
- Choose capacity_aware for steady-state workloads; focused_safety for new model releases; reservoir for exploratory audits.
4) Capacity planning (owner: SRE)
- Pre-allocate GPU pools for evald with a target headroom of 30% for burst.
5) Dry-run shadow (owner: ML Engineer)
- Run a 4-hour dry-run at 1% replication, inspect telemetry and ensure no production impacts.
6) Promote to full shadow (owner: product)
- Gradually increase replication to target; monitor fidelity deltas and capacity signals.

Regression triage fast path

If a regression is detected (fidelity_delta < threshold for critical slice):
1) Auto-throttle: Control Plane marks candidate as THROTTLED for new shadow replication.
2) Bisect: Launch a binary search over recent commits/quant profiles using the automated-regression-bisect assistant (see related page).
3) Localize slice: Use the eval-console to iterate on top-10 failing fingerprints and export 500 raw artifacts for human annotation.
4) Remediate: If regression is due to quant profile, revert to previous quant_profile for the slice or pin routing to baseline model_variant; file an incident per incident playbook.

Operational runbooks (runbook excerpt)

- Incident: Shadow-agent causing production latency increase
  1. SRE alert triggers when duplicate-path latency delta > 0.5ms sustained for 5 minutes.
  2. Run: curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/shadow/adjust --data '{"action":"throttle","target":"all"}'
  3. Verify production latency returns to baseline; roll back throttling only after 15 minutes of stable metrics.

Ownership and governance

- Ownership: ML Infrastructure owns Mirror Proxy + Sampler. Eval Platform team owns Eval Runner and Telemetry pipeline. Product/Applied ML owns slice definitions and acceptance criteria. SRE owns capacity and incident response.
- Review cadence: Quarterly reviews of fingerprint schema and sampling budgets. Post-release safety window: 14 days with elevated sampling on safety slices.

Privacy and retention notes

- PII redaction: The Mirroring Proxy must run the PII redaction pipeline for any customer with privacy_flag=true before storing payloads.
- Retention: Default retention is 30 days for shadow artifacts; extended retention requires customer consent and security review.

Appendices

A. Example fingerprint canonicalization pseudo-code

1. normalize = remove_dynamic_tokens(request.text)
2. redact = run_pii_redactor(normalize)
3. fingerprint = sha256(route_id + "|" + intent_class(redact) + "|" + length_bucket(redact))

B. Prioritized metric matrix (example)

- safety: false_negative_rate | threshold: < 0.01 | action: stop promotion
- semantic_fidelity: similarity_score | threshold: >= -0.02 | action: investigate if violated
- latency: p99 | threshold: increase < 0.5ms vs baseline | action: throttle shadowing

C. Frequently asked questions

Q: Will shadowing increase costs for the customer?
A: No customer-facing billing changes; internal cost is charged to platform evaluation budget. Customers can opt out per route.

Q: What if the shadow job reveals a reproducible bug?
A: Follow the regression triage fast path and open a public incident if customer-facing.

D. Related documents
- Shadow-to-prod eval continuity guidelines (link in related_pages)
- Heterogeneous hybrid quant deployment guidelines (link in related_pages)

Document change log

- 2024-07-12: Created by Aisha Romero (initial draft).
- 2025-10-18: Added differential-privacy sampling notes and capacity-aware throttling thresholds (review by Marcus Liu).
- 2025-11-02: Finalized acceptance criteria and CLI examples; published.

Title: Multi-tenant Shadow with Privacy Gating Playbook

Multi-tenant Shadow with Privacy Gating Playbook

Overview

This playbook defines Redwood's standard for running multi-tenant shadow evaluations with integrated privacy gating and redaction controls. It targets evaluation owners, SREs, and model-onboarding engineers who run shadow traffic for model promotion, quantization checks, and behaviour/regression detection across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals

- Exercise models on representative tenant traffic without exposing PII or violating privacy budgets.
- Detect regressions and quantization failures before promotion to production routes.
- Maintain isolation controls per-tenant and provide deterministic triage signals.
- Provide an auditable, repeatable orchestration pattern compatible with the eval-harness.

Terminology

- Shadow run: non-productive routing of real or synthetic requests to a candidate model variant for evaluation.
- Privacy gate: automated checks that block or truncate shadow requests containing sensitive content or that would exceed privacy budgets (DP epsilon, sample counts).
- Differential tenant seeding: sampling strategy that ensures each tenant’s probes are weighted while preserving k-anonymity thresholds.

Ownership and Roles

- Evaluation Owner: owns run config, probe set, and promotion decision (team: applied-ml).
- Shadow Operator (SRE): scopes routing policies, capacity, and rollout windows.
- Privacy Steward (Security/Privacy): approves DP budgets and redaction rules.
- Oncall (eng-sre): triages runtime anomalies during shadow runs.

Pre-run checklist (required)

| Item | Owner | Requirement | Accept/Block threshold |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Probe provenance & retention policy | Evaluation Owner | Define synthetic vs live probes, retention days | retained <= 30 days for live samples |
| DP budget allocation (epsilon) | Privacy Steward | Epsilon per-tenant / per-run | epsilon <= 1.0 for live-shadow; <= 2.5 for synthetic |
| Redaction schema | Privacy Steward | List of PII patterns to redact | All matched PII must be replaced with <REDACTED> |
| Tenant isolation policy | Shadow Operator | Max tenants per run, per-host | <= 50 tenants per cluster during high load |

Shadow Orchestration Procedure (step-by-step)

1) Prepare probe bundle: evaluation owner creates a bundle that includes `tenant_id`, `probe_id`, `probe_type` (live|synthetic), and `privacy_mask` flags. See Example bundle YAML below.

2) Determine sampling weights: run `probe-weighter` (internal tool) to compute per-tenant sampling such that at least k=5 distinct tenant probes exist per slice.

3) Apply privacy gating pre-filter: the `shadow-proxy` service must run the configured redaction rules and a DP sampler. If a probe fails gating (PII detected or sampler bucket full), it is dropped and recorded in `shadow-gate.log`.

4) Route to candidate variant(s): the router will forward to up to 3 concurrent candidate variants (A/B/n) with header `X-Shadow: true`. Ensure model container has `--shadow-mode` enabled to avoid metric pollution.

5) Telemetry capture: the eval-harness captures the following (min): `latency_ms`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `response_stability_index`, `embedding_cosine_delta`, `privacy_decision` (dropped/redacted/passed). Telemetry is written to `s3://eval-shadow/tenant=<tenant_id>/run=<run_id>/`.

6) Post-run automated checks:
   - Fidelity delta: if response_stability_index > 0.035 for any 5% tile, mark as 'fidelity-alert'.
   - Embedding shift: if mean embedding_cosine_delta > 0.04 for any intent-slice, flag for manual review.
   - Latency regressions: 95th percentile latency increase > 20% vs prod baseline triggers capacity/optimization run.

Privacy Gating Rules

- Redaction: PII regex patterns (SSN, credit_card, email, phone) must be censored. Example: replace digits with `#`.
- DP sampling: use randomized response with per-tenant epsilon budget. Track cumulative epsilon in `privacy-ledger`. If cumulative epsilon would exceed budget, block further live-shadow probes for that tenant for 24h.
- Synthetic-only fallback: if live probes are blocked by privacy gating, the system should automatically seed matched synthetic probes from the `probe-farm` to preserve coverage.
- Audit logging: every gating decision must include `reason_code` and `policy_id` and be stored for 365 days for compliance review.

Configuration table (recommended defaults)

| Config key | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| shadow.max_tenants_per_run | 50 | Protects isolation during heavy runs |
| shadow.max_requests_per_tenant_per_hour | 500 | Safety throttling |
| privacy.epsilon_live_per_run | 0.5 | Conservative default for live probes |
| privacy.dp_ledger_retention_days | 365 | Compliance requirement |
| metrics.fidelity_alert_threshold | 0.035 | Response stability index threshold |
| probes.synthetic_fallback_ratio | 1:1 | Synthetic probes seeded when live blocked |

Failure modes and triage playbook

- Failure: High fidelity alerts across multiple tenants.
  1. Triage owner: Evaluation Owner.
  2. Steps: compare probe slices, run deterministic replay in `shadow-replay` with seed control, check quantization profile for candidate variant.
  3. If replay reproduces, open model regression ticket `MRG-<run_id>` and attach samples and diff metrics.

- Failure: Privacy ledger overrun for tenant X.
  1. Triage owner: Privacy Steward + Shadow Operator.
  2. Steps: inspect `privacy-ledger` entries, rollback any synthetic promotions, notify tenant owner. Consider reducing probe rate or use aggregated probes.

- Failure: Latency tail regressions.
  1. Triage owner: Eng SRE.
  2. Steps: examine per-host load, increase capacity, profile kernel scheduling, consult `serving-runtime/profiling-playbook` (link below).

SLOs and Alerting

- Shadow-run completeness: >= 95% of requested probes executed (excluding privacy-blocked).
- Telemetry delivery SLO: 99.9% of events delivered to `s3` within 10 minutes.
- Privacy budget enforcement: 100% of gating decisions must be enforced and logged.

Promotion & Rollout Criteria

Promotion to canary or stage requires all of the following:
- No fidelity alerts in last 48h for production slices.
- Embedding shift within acceptable bound (mean_cosine_delta <= 0.03).
- Latency P95 within 10% of baseline.
- Privacy ledger shows available epsilon headroom for tenants involved.

Examples

Example probe bundle (YAML):

----
probe_bundle:
  run_id: "run-2026-02-10-42"
  tenant_id: "tenant-42"
  probes:
    - probe_id: "p-001"
      type: live
      input: "Customer request text..."
      privacy_mask: true
----

Run command (CLI):

$ redwood-eval run --bundle s3://eval-bundles/run-2026-02-10-42.yaml --env shadow --policy privacy-gating-v2 --out s3://eval-shadow/

Telemetry schema (minimal fields)

- run_id (string)
- tenant_id (string)
- probe_id (string)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- latency_ms (number)
- tokens_in (number)
- tokens_out (number)
- response_stability_index (number)
- embedding_cosine_delta (number)
- privacy_decision (string: passed|redacted|dropped)
- gating_reason (string, nullable)

Related pages and references

- eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026 (shadow continuity)
- regression-triage/drift-cache-interaction-investigation-playbook-2026 (cache/quant interactions)
- quantization-profiles/quant-impact-synthesis-for-prompt-families-2026 (quant checks)

Appendix: Implementation notes

- `shadow-proxy` must be deployed with a feature flag `privacy_gating_v2` and integrate with `privacy-ledger` via a transactional append API.
- Prefer deterministic seed control in synthetic probes to reproduce failures during triage.
- Alert metadata should include `run_id`, `slice_id`, and the top-3 contributing probes to speed debugging.

Contact and escalation

- Primary: Evelyn Park (applied-ml)
- Shadow infra: Samuel Li (eng-sre)
- Privacy steward: Priya Nair (security)

Revision history

- 2026-02-10: Initial publication by Evelyn Park.
- 2026-03-01: Updated gating thresholds and added synthetic-fallback ratio.

Title: Shadow Sequencer and Fallback Orchestration Playbook

Shadow Sequencer and Fallback Orchestration Playbook

Summary
-----
This playbook documents the Shadow Sequencer pattern and fallback orchestration used by the eval harness to safely validate new model variants (including quantized and trimmed kernels) across live workloads. It prescribes sequencing rules, sampling policies, telemetry contracts, and incident-runbook steps to keep production SLOs intact while maximizing signal for model onboarding and regression triage.

Audience
--------
- Applied ML engineers running model onboarding and continuous evals
- Serving runtime engineers integrating shadow pipelines
- SRE and platform teams responsible for routing and fallbacks

Goals
-----
1. Collect high-fidelity shadowed request/response pairs for evaluation without impacting user-perceived latency or correctness.
2. Provide deterministic sequencing and prioritization so limited eval capacity focuses on the most informative traffic slices.
3. Automate safe fallback to production variants on degradation (quality or latency).
4. Integrate with quantization and KV-cache-aware on-device evaluation flows.

Terminology
-----------
- Shadow request: a copy of a production request routed to an eval model for offline scoring and telemetry.
- Sequencer: the service that decides which production requests to shadow and at what priority. (service: eval-sequencer)
- Shadow bus: asynchronous pipeline that delivers shadow traffic to eval environments with metadata. (service: shadow-bus)
- Fallback policy: policy that triggers automatic rollback or traffic diversion when a health gate fails.

Architecture overview
---------------------
1. Production ingress -> routing layer (redwood-router).
2. redwood-router emits a sampling key and forwards the request to production model variant.
3. eval-sequencer subscribes to routing metadata and decides shadow eligibility using the Sequencing Policy DB (see configs).
4. Eligible requests are serialized and posted to shadow-bus (Kafka topic: shadows.v1) with encryption and a metadata envelope.
5. Shadow consumers (dedicated eval-pools, private shadow runners) pull and run model variants; results written to eval-store and linked back to the originating request id for later comparison.

Sequencing policy (high level)
-----------------------------
- Priority classes (in descending order):
  - P0: production slow-paths and SLA-critical endpoints (sample rate: 0.1% default)
  - P1: high-business-value cohorts (paid customers, sample rate: 1%)
  - P2: high-entropy prompts (identified by probe classifier, sample rate: 5%)
  - P3: heavy compute or long-context examples (sample rate: 0.5%)
- Global budget: max 3% of total QPS can be shadowed into any single eval-cluster to avoid resource interference.
- Adaptive throttle: sample rates are dynamically lowered if the eval-cluster CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for 5m window.

Sequencing config table (editable YAML snippet)
------------------------------------------------
| key | meaning | recommended value |
|-----|---------|-------------------|
| sequencer.default_rate | baseline sampling | 0.01 |
| sequencer.priority_p1_rate | paid customers | 0.01 |
| sequencer.max_cluster_shadow_pct | cap per cluster | 0.03 |
| sequencer.cpu_util_throttle_pct | throttling threshold | 0.75 |

(Example YAML for a sequence rule)
```yaml
- id: p1_paid_customers
  match: request.customer_tier == \"paid\"
  sample_rate: 0.01
  priority: P1
  destinations: [\"eval-dedicated-a\", \"eval-private-vpc\"]
```

Security and privacy controls
-----------------------------
- All shadow payloads are hashed at ingress and PII fields redacted according to the redaction ruleset (service: pii-filter).
- Shadow bus messages are encrypted with customer-scoped keys; private deployment shadows can be configured to never persist in central eval-store.
- For regulated customers, use DP-mode: add Laplace noise to numeric telemetry and strip verbatim user content before storage.

Telemetry and SLOs
------------------
- Critical SLOs that must not be violated by shadowing:
  - P99 production latency change: <= +1.5ms attributable to shadowing hooks.
  - Error budget: shadow subsystem must not cause >0.1% increase in 5xx rate.
- Observability outputs:
  - metric: eval.shadowed_requests_count (tags: priority, destination, model_variant)
  - metric: eval.shadow_processing_lag_seconds (95th)
  - log: shadow-envelope-{request_id} includes: request_id, sampling_key, model_variant, seq_rule, cluster_id

Quality gates and automated fallback triggers
-------------------------------------------
We evaluate shadow-run results weekly and in near real-time for the following gates. Any failure above thresholds triggers one of the fallback actions below.

Quality gates (examples)
- Token-level degradation: LM_delta_bleu > 0.12 vs baseline for customer-critical prompts
- Latency regressions: 95th percentile increase > 15% for the model variant under test
- Regression alerts per 10k shadowed requests > 3

Fallback actions (ranked)
1. Circuit-breaker: stop all new shadowing for the failing variant for 30 minutes.
2. Auto-rollforward: if degradation persists and a compatible fallback exists (quantized->float or small->large), route canary traffic to fallback variant with gradual ramping.
3. Live rollback: for Dedicated or Private deployments with observed customer impact, automatically switch traffic away from the failing variant at the routing layer and create incident.

Operational runbook (incident scenario: spike in token degradation)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Triage: PagerDuty -> oncall-eng (eval). Confirm spike via grafana: eval.quality.regression_rate (5m).
2. Identify sequencer keys correlated with regressions via:
   - CLI: rcli seq-query --from 2026-03-02T09:00Z --to 2026-03-02T09:30Z --filter=regression=1
3. Stop shadowing for the implicated variant:
   - curl -XPOST https://eval-sequencer/api/v1/rules/disable -d '{"rule_id":"<id>"}'
4. If spike persists > 30m, enable fallback route to previous stable variant:
   - rcli routes update --route-id prod-chat --fallback-variant redwood-gpt-3b-stable --weight 100
5. Postmortem: capture root-cause, model diff, and submit to regression-triage workspace.

Integration checklist for model onboarding
----------------------------------------
- Ensure the model is registered in model-catalog with the following metadata: variant_id, quant_profile, kv_cache_compatibility, expected_latency_ms.
- Attach an eval-suite that includes: production prompt slices, adversarial probes, and a small human-labeled gold set for P1 customers.
- Verify shadow-run: run 1k synthetic shadow requests using the shadow-runner utility:
  - shadow-runner --variant <id> --sample-size 1000 --emulate-headers
- Confirm telemetry: eval.shadowed_requests_count > 1000 and eval.quality.sentinal_pass == true

Operational tips (best practices)
--------------------------------
- Prefer deterministic hashing for stable slice selection to enable reproducible comparisons.
- Use higher sampling for rare high-value slices (e.g., B2B integrations) and lower sampling for generic low-value traffic.
- For quantized variants, annotate messages with quant_profile to enable downstream analysts to compare like-for-like.

Example CLI snippets
--------------------
- Create a new sequencing rule:
  rcli sequencer create --name p2_high_entropy --match-file p2_match.json --sample-rate 0.05 --destinations eval-dedicated-a
- Disable shadowing for a variant immediately:

Title: Shadow Rollforward and Mesh Simulation Playbook

Shadow Rollforward and Mesh Simulation Playbook

Overview and purpose:

This playbook documents the Shadow Rollforward and Mesh Simulation pattern: a structured, low-risk pathway for validating model upgrades, quantized variants, and routing policy changes using a combination of shadow traffic, synthetic mesh simulations, and progressive rollforward rules. It complements the standard canary/cutover runbooks by emphasizing reproducible simulation meshes, cost-sensitive quant variants, and automated failure classification to shorten time-to-safe-promotion.

Who should use this:
- ML engineers preparing model promotions from staging to production
- SRE and platform engineers owning rollout automation and routing policies
- Applied ML / evaluation teams designing eval harness integrations

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to text generation, chat, and embedding routes that support shadow mirroring and model variant routing.
- Not intended for datasets that contain regulated PII unless Private deployment controls are in place.
- Requires the evaluation harness to be able to replay requests deterministically (see Pre-reqs).

Definitions:
- Shadow Rollforward: Gradual promotion path where new model variants receive mirrored traffic and simulated production meshes before taking live traffic.
- Mesh Simulation: Orchestrated synthetic traffic generator that reshapes request distributions (context lengths, few-shot examples, system prompts) to emulate production slices.

Prerequisites:
1) Promotion artifacts:
   - Signed model bundle (model-id, sha256, quant-profile) stored in model registry.
   - Evaluation report with slice-level metrics and accepted thresholds.
2) Platform capabilities:
   - Shadow mirroring enabled at route level and/or request proxy.
   - Canary and rollout policy engine accessible (canary weight scheduling, automatic rollback hooks).
   - Evaluation harness with seedable RNG and replay mode.
3) Observability:
   - Per-route token-level latency and cost tracking in Redwood Console.
   - Quality monitors (ROUGE/BLEU approximations, semantic similarity, hallucination detectors) hooked into alerting.

Key components in the pattern:
- Shadow router: duplicates production requests to candidate model(s) with adjustable sampling.
- Mesh simulator: synthesizes permutations of request context (prompt perturbation, prefix cache hit/miss simulation, dynamic shots).
- Quant variant manager: assigns quantization profile and GPU/backing variant used for experiments.
- Evaluator: aggregates shadow responses, computes metrics, and performs automatic regression classification (statistical and heuristic checks).

Acceptance criteria and SLOs (examples):
| Metric                             | Target (pass/fail)                       | Alert threshold | Action on breach |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-----------------|------------------|
| Overall semantic similarity (avg) | >= 0.88 cosine to golden responses       | < 0.86          | Halt promotion   |
| Latency (p95, generation only)    | <= 450ms on dedicated tier               | > 600ms         | Revert variant   |
| Token cost delta                   | <= +12% vs baseline (same throughput)    | > +20%          | Investigate cost policy |
| Hallucination rate (slice top10)  | <= baseline + 1.5%                       | +2.5%           | Reject promotion |
| Stability index (answer churn)    | <= 0.05 increase                          | > 0.08          | Run deeper triage |

Note: Use slice-driven evaluation—measure per-customer, per-intent, and per-context-length buckets.

Mesh simulation design checklist:
- Identify 6–10 representative slices from production telemetry (e.g., helpdesk-paraphrase, code-completion, long-context summarization).
- For each slice, enumerate perturbations: template paraphrases, token masking, extra-system prompts, prefix cache warm/cold states.
- Define weightings to reflect production frequency and business criticality (weights must sum to 1).
- Add failure injections: truncated responses, partial KV-cache misses, and latency spikes to observe graceful degradation.

Procedure: Shadow Rollforward + Mesh Simulation (step-by-step)
1) Prepare artifacts and baseline: 
   - Lock baseline model version id and collect 24–72h telemetry for target routes.
   - Generate golden responses on a fixed seed set via eval harness.
2) Configure mesh: 
   - Create a mesh definition file that maps slices -> perturbations -> sample weights. See example below.
3) Deploy candidate model to a shadow-only endpoint (no live routing) with quant profiles set per the experiment.
4) Start shadow mirroring at 5% of production QPS. Mirror sampling should stratify by slice.
5) Run mesh simulation for N=12h or until the sample size per slice meets statistical power (min 500 examples per slice recommended).
6) Evaluate metrics using the evaluator; run both deterministic and stochastic checks (multi-seed aggregation).
7) Run regression classification: automatic triage should label any significant regressions into categories (semantic, latency/cost, instability, hallucination).
8) If pass, transition to progressive rollforward: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over successive windows with continuous shadowing of additional variants.
9) If fail, trigger fast rollback and automatic issue report creation with attached logs, sample traces, and a reproducible mesh replay spec.

Mesh definition example (YAML excerpt):

# mesh-definition.yaml
# top-level: slices with perturbations and weights
slices:
  - name: "support_paraphrase"
    weight: 0.28
    perturbations:
      - paraphrase_template: 10
      - add_system_prompt: 5
      - cold_kv_cache: 1
  - name: "long_context_summary"
    weight: 0.24
    perturbations:
      - truncate_context: 3
      - add_irrelevant_paragraph: 2
      - increased_shots: 1
  - name: "code_completion"
    weight: 0.12
    perturbations:
      - masked_tokens: 5
      - varying_indent: 1

Reproducible commands and snippets:
- Run mesh simulator (CLI):
  rwd-mesh simulate --mesh mesh-definition.yaml --samples 20000 --seed 42 --output ./mesh-results.json

- Start shadow mirroring (kubectl example for ingress config):
  kubectl patch configroute redwood-routing -p '{"spec": {"shadowPercent":5, "shadowTargets":[{"model":"candidate-v2","quant_profile":"q4_0"}]}}'

- Extract evaluator summary (python snippet):
  from rwd_eval import Aggregator
  agg = Aggregator('./mesh-results.json')
  report = agg.slice_summary(metrics=['cosine_sim','p95_latency','hallucination_rate'])
  print(report.to_markdown())

Failure classification and automated triage rules (examples):
- Rule A: If semantic similarity drops > 0.06 on any slice and p-value < 0.01 => label semantic_regression, priority P0.
- Rule B: If p95 latency increases > 30% and absolute p95 > 600ms => label perf_regression, throttle rollforward.
- Rule C: If hallucination_rate increases by >1.5% absolute on customer-critical slices => automatic rollback and notify safety team.

Runbook: immediate actions on regression detection:
1) Pause rollout and set traffic weight to 0 for candidate.
2) Re-run deterministic mesh replay with identical RNG seeds to confirm.
3) Run pairwise diff between baseline and candidate responses for failing slice and store sample IDs.
4) Notify owner (tagged on alert) and collect GPU/VM perf counters, kernel logs, and cache hit trace.
5) If cause is quantization (identified by increased instability in short-context samples), re-run with next-higher precision quant profile and re-evaluate.

Quantization-specific guidance:
- Always include at least one higher-precision fallback (e.g., q8_0) in the shadow mesh to isolate quant noise vs model logic changes.
- Use multi-seed aggregation to reveal nondeterministic token churn introduced by lower-precision kernels.
- Monitor KV-cache interaction: some quant kernels exhibit disproportionate instability on cold cache sequences. Include cold/warm cache perturbations explicitly.

Observability checklist (what to record):
- Request-level: request_id, slice_id, prompt_hash, seed, route, model_id, quant_profile.
- Response-level: full response, tokenization map, per-token latencies, logits (if available), KV-cache-hit boolean.
- System-level: GPU utilization, IPC, kernel choice, memory pressure, swap events.

Promotion playbook: when to roll forward fully
- Pass criteria met for 72h of continuous mesh simulation + shadow validation across all critical slices.
- No P0 regressions; all P1 triages resolved with mitigation plans.
- Cost delta within approved threshold and fallback path validated.
- Observability hooks and audit logging confirmed in Private and Dedicated deployments.

Post-promotion monitoring and stability windows:
- Post-promote stabilize window: 7 days with elevated sampling of critical customers and a shadow copy of previous baseline for 24/7 comparison.
- Run scheduled deep-eval at 24h, 72h, and 7d marks; include multi-seed aggregation and variance budgeting.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary: model-owner (ML Engineer) — responsible for artifact and eval paper trail.
- Secondary: platform-sre — manage rollout automation and revert.
- Tertiary: applied-ml-evals — owns mesh definitions, evaluator tooling, and final acceptance.
- Escalation path: on P0 breach notify oncall -> SRE lead -> Head of Applied ML within 30 minutes.

Audit and reproducibility:
- Always store mesh-definition.yaml, eval harness seed files, and raw shadow-results in the model registry entry for the candidate model.
- Attach a minimal reproducible replay bundle to the incident ticket: includes seed set, environment digest, and exact rollout policy.

Appendix A: Example quick checklist (for on-shift engineers)
- [ ] Verify mesh-definition exists and slice weights reflect current traffic.
- [ ] Confirm evaluator suite passes smoke tests locally with baseline.
- [ ] Start mirror at 5% and validate sample distribution after first 10 minutes.
- [ ] Ensure observability streams (latency, tokens, hallucination detector) are live.
- [ ] Run summarized report and confirm no P0/P1 regressions before increasing weight.

Appendix B: FAQ
Q: How long should each rollforward window be?
A: Minimum 4 hours for low-volume routes; 12–24 hours for high-variance or customer-critical slices. Use statistical power calculation to determine sample adequacy.

Q: Can we reuse existing eval prompt sets?
A: Yes, but they must be augmented with mesh perturbations to expose cache interactions and quant instability.

Q: Is it safe to use shadow results for billing/cost estimates?
A: Only approximate—shadow runs are often sampled and may not reflect production caching/latency exactly. Use dedicated perf tests for accurate cost measurement.

- KV-cache quant stability audit playbook (internal)
- Regression investigation handbook (internal)

Title: Eval mesh topology and slotting cookbook

Eval mesh topology and slotting cookbook

Overview:
This cookbook defines the recommended topology, slotting strategies, and operational patterns for the eval mesh used across Redwood’s evaluation fleet. The document covers: mesh topology patterns, slot types and sizing; the slot allocation algorithm; cost and fidelity accounting; backfill and rebalancing strategies; safety and privacy gates for shadow workloads; and an operational runbook for deploying topology changes.

Goals:
- Provide a predictable, cost-aware mapping from eval workloads (probes, shadow traffic, backfills) to scarce evaluation capacity.
- Minimize eval latency for high-priority probes while maximizing overall probe coverage within budget.
- Ensure safe rollouts and auditable chargebacks for tenant-aware evals.

Audience:
- Evaluation platform engineers (owners of eval-orch and shadow-mesh).
- Onboarding engineers preparing probe manifests and budgets.
- SREs responsible for eval fleet capacity and cost allocation.

Key services and components:
- eval-orch: central orchestrator that assigns probes to slots and emits allocation events.
- probe-fabricator: generates synthetic probes and seeds shadow traffic.
- shadow-mesh: per-cluster runtime that executes shadow workloads; supports isolation modes (tenant, mixed, anonymized).
- telemetry-ingest: collects token-level latency/cost/time-series for evals.
- eval-ledger: accounting service that records slot consumption and cost attributions.

Definitions:
1) Slot: a reserved execution slot on the eval mesh. Slots have attributes: tier, cpu/gpu profile, qps limit, and cost weight.
2) Probe class: a logically grouped set of probes (e.g., functioncall-stability, longcontext-coherence, embedding-drift).
3) Fidelity budget: the allocation of high-fidelity slots for a probe class over a time window.

Topology patterns (recommended):
A) Hierarchical mesh (default) — used for most workloads:
   - Global control plane (eval-orch) + regional shadow-mesh clusters.
   - Each regional mesh exposes three slot pools: fast (low-latency), steady (balanced), bulk (throughput-optimized).
   - Routing policy: prefer local fast -> local steady -> cross-region steady -> bulk.

B) Isolated shadow mesh (sensitive tenants) — for regulated customers:
   - Dedicated shadow cluster with tenant-only slots and KMS-protected probes.
   - No cross-tenant colocation; telemetry scrubbed at source.

Slot types and sizing (reference table):
| slot_type | cpu/gpu | qps_limit | median_latency_target | cost_weight | recommended_use_cases |
| fast      | 1xA100 | 50       | < 40ms                | 5x         | interactive probes, micro-canaries |
| steady    | 1xA100 | 200      | < 120ms               | 2x         | baseline continuous probes        |
| bulk      | 2xA100 | 1000     | best-effort            | 1x         | backfills, large-scale simulations|

Slot allocation algorithm (summary):
1. Ingest probe manifest with metadata: priority (P0..P3), fidelity_required (high/medium/low), probe_weight, tenant_id, SLA_window.
2. Compute effective score = priority_weight * fidelity_multiplier / expected_tokens_per_probe.
3. Run candidate selection: try to place in same-region fast pool if score >= fast_threshold; otherwise steady; if no fit and probe is low-fidelity, schedule into bulk with sampling.
4. Perform cost check against probe class fidelity budget in eval-ledger; if budget overrun, enqueue for token-sampled run or reject with recommendation.

Allocation heuristics and thresholds (tunable knobs):
- priority_weight: P0=1.0 (critical), P1=0.6, P2=0.3, P3=0.1
- fidelity_multiplier: high=1.0, medium=0.6, low=0.2
- fast_threshold: 0.7
- steady_threshold: 0.3
- backfill_sampling_rate (for bulk): default 0.05 (5%)

Cost and fidelity accounting:
- Eval-ledger records: slot_id, probe_manifest_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_processed, cost_estimate.
- Monthly billing export includes: tenant_id, probe_class, total_tokens, slot-weighted-cost.
- Fidelity budget alerts: generate when projected spend > 80% of allocated monthly fidelity budget for probe class.

Backfill and rebalancing policy:
- Trigger conditions: underutilization > 20% for 15m OR overload (queue depth > 2000).
- Backfill steps:
  1) Identify candidate low-priority low-fidelity probes for bulk migration.
  2) Apply progressive sampling ramp (0% -> 5% -> 25% over 30m) with telemetry gates.
  3) Monitor fidelity signal (response-stability-index, latency-tail) — abort if degradation > configured delta.
- Rebalancing (auto): every 10 minutes, eval-orch computes target distribution and migrates slots with live cutover window of 2 minutes.

Safety, privacy, and gating:
- All shadow traffic must be redacted by probe-fabricator before entering telemetry-ingest.
- Sensitive-probe flag triggers isolated shadow-mesh placement.
- Rollout gating: new topology rules must pass canary on 3 regional meshes for at least 24h with no fidelity or latency regression > 2x baseline.

Operational runbook: topology change flow
1) Draft topology change PR (config: pools, thresholds, weightings) and post to #eval-ops.
2) Create an experiment manifest in eval-orch with scope=canary (regions: us-west-2, eu-central-1).
3) Dry-run allocation for 24h (simulation mode) and gather: slot fill curves, projected ledger spend, telemetry delta.
4) If dry-run passes, enable canary with 1% of global probe volume for 24h.
5) Escalation criteria (immediately rollback if any fires):
   - fidelity_delta > 3% for P0 probes
   - latency tail (p99) increase > 150ms for fast slots
   - spending rate > 2x projection
6) Gradually increase canary (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with 12h observation windows between steps.

Example slotting config (YAML example):
---
slot_pools:
  - name: fast
    gpu: a100-40gb
    concurrency: 50
    weight: 5
    allocation_threshold: 0.7
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
  - name: steady
    gpu: a100-40gb
    concurrency: 200
    weight: 2
    allocation_threshold: 0.3
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
  - name: bulk
    gpu: 2xa100
    concurrency: 1000
    weight: 1
    sampling_rate: 0.05
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
---

Probe manifest fields (example):
- probe_id: pc-2026-485
- probe_class: longcontext-coherence-v2
- priority: P1
- fidelity_required: high
- expected_tokens: 1200
- sensitive: false
- owner: search-team@redwood.ai

Telemetry and alerting knobs to configure for topology rollouts:
- response-stability-index (RSI) delta alert: > 2x baseline -> sev-2
- p99 latency increase (fast slots): > 150ms -> sev-2
- fidelity-budget burn rate: projected > 80% -> paging to cost-ops
- slot-fill anomaly (< 10% utilization across 30m) -> investigate potential overprovisioning

Debugging checklist (when probes are not scheduled or fail):
1) Check eval-orch allocation logs for allocation_reject reasons.
2) Query eval-ledger for probe_manifest_id and cost budget status.
3) Inspect shadow-mesh metrics for slot health (oom_count, preemptions, avg_qps).
4) If privacy gating blocked allocation, confirm probe redaction passed (probe-fabricator logs).

Rollout example (real case study):
- Goal: reduce cost for continuous functioncall-stability probes by 18% while preserving p99 latency for P0 canaries.
- Action: introduced a new steady pool with 1.5x concurrency and weight=1.8, enabled progressive bulk sampling for low-fidelity sub-slices.
- Result: after staged rollout (1% -> 20% -> 100%), observed 17.9% cost reduction and p99 for P0 canaries remained within 8ms of baseline.

Ownership and contacts:
- Owners: eval-platform team (primary), evaluation-costing (secondary).
- Oncall: eval-sre rotation (pager: #eval-oncall).
- Escalation path: eval-oncall -> eval-platform -> platform-sre -> eng-lead.

Appendix A — tuning knobs and recommended defaults:
- fast_threshold: 0.7
- steady_threshold: 0.3
- backfill_sampling_rate: 0.05
- fidelity_alert_pct: 80
- rebalancing_interval_minutes: 10
- canary_step_windows: [24h, 12h, 12h]

Title: Evaluator Onboarding and Certification Curriculum - 2026

Evaluator Onboarding and Certification Curriculum - 2026

Purpose

This page defines the official Redwood Evaluation Team curriculum for onboarding, certifying, and re-certifying evaluators who operate the eval harness, curate prompt/probe suites, and run shadow/federated experiments across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The curriculum is designed to: 1) shorten time-to-productivity, 2) reduce annotation and probe creation variance, 3) ensure consistent use of quantification and regression triage tools, and 4) codify the certification gates that allow an evaluator to approve production shadow runs.

Audience

- New evaluators joining the Applied ML group.
- ML engineers responsible for shadow validation and probe orchestration.
- Cross-functional reviewers (SRE/product) who sign off on production gating.

Overview and outcomes

At the end of the curriculum, an evaluator will be able to:
- Operate the Eval Harness CLI and submit reproducible probe runs (eval-mesh).
- Compose probe families that cover calibration, drift, long-tail, and quant-sensitivity slices.
- Run a shadow-to-prod migration with the Probe Migration Checklist and pass the certification exam.
- Diagnose regressions using the Regression Investigation Playbook and bootstrap a quant-fallback experiment.

Structure

The curriculum has three phased tracks that must be completed in sequence:

1) Foundations (2 weeks) — orientation, tooling, safety basics
2) Applied Labs (3 weeks) — hands-on probe design, shadow runs, annotation calibration
3) Certification and Audit (1 week) — exam, live run approval, pairing audit

Each phase contains lectures, reading, a set of hands-on tasks, and acceptance criteria. Evaluators are paired with a "steward" (senior evaluator) for at least one full shadow lifecycle.

Phase 1: Foundations (2 weeks)

Goal: Ensure the evaluator understands the platform, core telemetry, and quality guardrails.

Mandatory reading and videos:
- "Eval Harness Primer" (internal video, 35m)
- "Quality Guardrails: SQC mapping" (doc)
- "KV-cache behavior and quant sensitivity" (paper summary)

Access & setup checklist:
1. Request access to eval-mesh and probe-fabricator via internal ticket (Tool-Access-202).
2. Verify RBAC: membership in group redwood-evaluators and read access to eval-telemetry.
3. Complete online safety course (security-and-compliance/module-eval-safety).

Local environment quickstart (required):
- Install evaluator-cli: pip install redwood-evaluator-cli==0.6.1
- Configure credentials: evaluator configure --profile sandbox --region us-west-2
- Run a smoke probe: evaluator run --probe-id sample/smoke-001 --mode dry-run

Acceptance criteria (foundations):
- Can run a dry-run without errors and retrieve telemetry IDs.
- Pass a short quiz (min score 80%) covering SLOs, confidentiality rules, and probe privacy budget.

Phase 2: Applied Labs (3 weeks)

Goal: Practice probe authoring, slice definition, annotation calibration, and shadow execution across quantized and unquantized model variants.

Core modules and exercises:
A. Probe Design Lab (3 exercises)
- Exercise 1: Build a calibration probe family for the "fewshot-summarization" workflow. Deliverables: JSON probe manifest, expected anchors, and acceptance tests.
- Exercise 2: Create a long-context cohesion probe that stresses KV cache boundaries. Deliverables: token-length distribution, expected failure modes, and a seed corpus.
- Exercise 3: Design a perturbation probe to surface quant-induced hallucination modes. Deliverables: perturbation matrix and repair template.

B. Annotation Calibration & Economics (2 exercises)
- Calibrate three annotators using the Annotator Calibration Toolkit. Target inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff alpha) >= 0.75 for high-signal slices.
- Run an annotation budget exercise: plan cost for 5k judgments across three slices and optimize for efficiency (heuristic: prioritize high-impact seeds).

C. Shadow Run Execution (live pairing with steward)
- Perform an end-to-end shadow run against model family: rwin-13b (float16), rwin-13b-q4 (quant), and rwin-7b (fallback).
- Follow the Shadow Run Checklist (see table below) while steward pairs for run sign-off.

Shadow Run Checklist (table)

| Step | Responsible | Artifact | Threshold/Notes |
|------|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| Probe manifest review | Evaluator + Steward | manifest.yaml | All probes have anchor coverage >= 90% |
| Dry-run verification | Evaluator | smoke logs | No runtime errors; 95th latency < 1.2x baseline |
| Annotation plan approved | Evaluator | annotation-plan.md | Annotator QA plan included; privacy budget specified |
| Metric contract set | Evaluator | eval-contract.json | Primary metric and delta budget defined (see Metric Contracts) |
| Run approval | Steward | run-id | Steward signs after drift/fidelity checks |

Metric Contracts (example)
- Primary metric: Response Coherence (rc_score) computed by evaluator-metrics v1.4
- Acceptance gate: rc_score delta >= -0.015 relative to baseline OR pass compensating slice checks
- Latency SLO: p95 infer latency <= 240ms for 128-token average length on dedicated pool

Commands and example manifests

Example manifest manifest.yaml (snippet):

```
probe_family: summarization_calibration_v2
model_targets:
  - rwin-13b
  - rwin-13b-q4
slices:
  - name: anchor_examples
    seed_source: corpus/summaries/anchor-2025
    expected_pass_rate: 0.92
  - name: long_context_priming
    seed_source: corpus/long/slice-a
    expected_pass_rate: 0.88
```

Run command (example):
- evaluator run --manifest manifest.yaml --priority normal --dry-run=false --telemetry-tag evaluator/onboarding/$(whoami)

Acceptance criteria (applied labs):
- Manifest and probe families reviewed by steward.
- Shadow runs produced telemetry and produced pass/fail slices as predicted for >= 3 of 4 probes.
- Annotator calibration passes (alpha >= 0.75) for primary slices.

Phase 3: Certification and Audit (1 week)

Goal: Demonstrate independent run ownership and the ability to approve a shadow run for promotion to canary stage.

Components:
1) Written exam (open book) — 60 minutes, passing score 85%. Topics: metric contract writing, privacy budget, probe manifest conventions, rollback criteria.
2) Practical exam — run ownership: the candidate must design and execute a configuration that flips on a new quantized variant via the staging mesh and demonstrate the ability to trigger a safe rollback.
3) Audit pairing — candidate does a live run while a cross-team reviewer (SRE or Product) monitors.

Practical exam rubric (summary):
- Correctness of probe manifests: 30 pts
- Metric contract defensibility and thresholds: 25 pts
- Annotation pipeline and QA: 20 pts
- Rollback and mitigation plan: 25 pts
- Passing threshold: >= 80/100

Certification outcomes and badges
- Certified Evaluator — full sign-off: allowed to approve shadow runs for canary (limited to one model family until first three live canaries are monitored). Badge granted in HR profile and redwood-evaluators group.
- Provisional Evaluator — passed practical but needs two additional steward-signed runs to be upgraded.

Re-certification and continuing education (annual)
- All certified evaluators must re-certify yearly by: 1) completing a 4-hour update on new tooling/metrics, and 2) passing a short practical re-cert exercise.
- If a major change (e.g., new quant scheme, new KV cache architecture) is introduced, temporary re-cert drives may be required: stewards will notify via #eval-ops.

Operational integrants and run governance

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Applied ML — Eval Team (owner_team: engineering)
- Steward role: senior evaluator assigned per-model-family; contact via steward-oncall rotation
- Escalation path: evaluator -> steward -> model-owner -> SRE -> oncall-exec

Approval gates for promotion to production canary:
1. Metric contract satisfied within delta budgets.
2. No high-severity slice failures (severity defined in Failure Taxonomy doc).
3. Annotation QA completed and auditable.
4. SRE performance smoke tests passed (p95 latency within agreed SLA).

Tooling references and troubleshooting

- evaluator-cli docs: internal link /tools/evaluator-cli (version 0.6+ required)
- eval-mesh run logs: run logs available in Kibana under index eval-mesh-logs-*
- Telemetry quick query (example):
  curl -s "https://telemetry-api.internal/v1/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"run_id":"<RUN_ID>","metrics":["rc_score","latency_p95"]}' | jq

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Symptom: p95 latency spike in quant variant
  Mitigation: trigger fallback to non-quant variant and file a performance incident; capture runtime kernels and attach to triage ticket.
- Symptom: Annotator drift (Krippendorff alpha < 0.6)
  Mitigation: pause annotation, recalibrate annotators using gold set, re-run sample.
- Symptom: Metric contract violation on minority slice
  Mitigation: Evaluate slice-specific compensating checks; if multiple high-priority slices fail, rollback.

Appendix A — Suggested onboarding schedule (4-week calendar)

Week 0: Pre-boarding
- Access requests, install CLI, watch primer video.
Week 1: Foundations
- Read docs, pass quiz, complete dry-run.

Title: Cohort-driven Shadow Validation Playbook

Cohort-driven Shadow Validation Playbook

Overview:

This playbook describes a repeatable, cohort-driven approach to shadow (non-production) validation that combines traffic mirroring, cohort stratification, and statistical evaluation to detect drift, regressions, or QoE degradations before a model rollout. It is intended for use by ML Engineers, Product Reliability, and SRE when validating model variants (quantized models, finetunes, or new topologies) against real traffic slices.

Goals:
- Expose subtle, slice-specific regressions that aggregate metrics miss.
- Provide deterministic acceptance gates with clear thresholds and statistical tests.
- Keep validation cost-bounded by adaptive sampling and prioritized cohorts.

Scope and Non-Goals:
- Scope: live shadowing and replay for text-generation and embedding endpoints; cohort metrics for latency, token cost, response-stability, and semantic fidelity.
- Non-Goals: synthetic adversarial fuzzing (see separate fuzz playbook) and complete production failover automation.

Definitions:
- Shadow traffic: duplicated requests sent to a candidate model without impacting production responses.
- Cohort: a named subset of traffic defined by request attributes (customer_id, route, prompt-template, language, token_count, session_age).
- Response-stability-index (RSI): composite metric measuring output drift against baseline using embedding cosine similarity, edit distance, and semantic score.

When to run a cohort-driven shadow validation:
- Before a model promotion that affects >5% of production request volume.
- When introducing cross-workload optimizations (e.g., new quant profile, KV-cache changes, batch scheduling).
- After detecting slice-specific degradations in continuous telemetry.

Ownership and Roles:
- Requesting owner: Feature/Model owner (creates cohorts and success criteria).
- Shadow operator: SRE / Infra (sets up mirroring, monitors resource usage).
- Evaluator: Applied ML / Quality (runs statistical tests, interprets slice failures).
- Approver: Product owner or Reliability lead (approves promotion or rollback).

High-level Workflow (stepwise):
1) Define cohorts (3–10 per run):
   - Use historical telemetry to choose meaningful slices (high-value customers, long-context, multimodal inputs).
   - Example cohort definitions: "high-long-context-english" (tokens > 2048), "enterprise-integration-route" (route = /api/v1/generate && customer_tier = enterprise).
2) Choose sampling policy and budget:
   - Default: mirror 10% of cohort traffic for 72 hours or until 5,000 requests per cohort are collected, whichever comes first.
   - For sensitive cohorts, reduce to 1–2% with extended duration.
3) Configure shadow routing (example manifest):
   - Provide network-level mirroring rules and candidate endpoint. See appendix for JSON/YAML snippets.
4) Instrument telemetry and tagging:
   - Ensure every mirrored request is tagged with: cohort_id, shadow_run_id, baseline_model, candidate_model, sample_rate.
   - Log raw prompts, token counts, latency, final cost estimate (tokens * model_cost_rate).
5) Compute per-cohort metrics (real-time and batch):
   - Latency P95 and P99 (ms).
   - Token cost delta (%).
   - RSI (median per cohort) and drift fraction (percent responses with RSI < threshold).
   - Functional correctness checks: reranking loss, presence/absence of required fields for structured outputs.
6) Statistical evaluation and thresholds:
   - For continuous metrics (latency, cost): use bootstrap confidence intervals with 10k resamples. Gate if candidate P99 > baseline P99 + 20% and p < 0.01.
   - For semantic/fidelity metrics (RSI): require median RSI >= baseline median - 0.03 and two-sided Mann-Whitney U test p > 0.05.
   - For categorical regressions (required fields missing): Fisher exact test, require failure rate delta < 0.5 percentage points with 95% CI.
7) Adaptive triage and probe amplification:
   - If a cohort shows borderline failure (0.01 < p < 0.05), automatically increase sampling for that cohort by up to 5x for an additional 24 hours.
8) Runbook actions on failures:
   - Soft fail (slice flagged): pause promotion, notify owners, request focused remediation (prompt-tune, quant-fix, dataset augmentation).
   - Hard fail (critical customer slice degraded or functional correctness violated): immediate rollback path and incident creation.
9) Promotion decision and documentation:
   - Successful run: produce a validation artifact containing per-cohort summaries, raw probe examples (anonymized), and final decision. Attach to release ticket.

Metric and Alerting Configuration (table):
| Metric | Aggregation | Gate | Action on breach | Ownership |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Latency P99 | per-cohort | > baseline + 20% (p<0.01) | Pause promotion, trigger perf triage | SRE |
| Token cost delta | median % | > +15% | Cost review, consider quant profile | Finance/Feature owner |
| RSI median | median similarity | < baseline - 0.03 (MWU p<0.05) | Quality investigation, escalate | Applied ML |
| Required-field loss | failure rate | delta > 0.005 absolute | Immediate rollback for critical routes | Product |

Sampling and Budgeting Guidelines:
- Minimum sample per cohort for significance: 500 requests. If unavailable, mark cohort as "insufficient data" and schedule an extended run.
- Budget cap per run: token budget defined in run config (default 10M tokens). Operator may truncate tests if budget exhausted and annotate results.

Data Privacy and Redaction:
- Always redact PII before storing mirrored requests. Use the pipeline redaction rules: replace emails, SSNs, API keys, and long identifiers with deterministic tokens.
- For enterprise customers with confidentiality flags, request explicit authorization before mirroring; otherwise exclude those cohorts.

Operational Playbook (quick steps):
1) Create run ticket with cohort definitions and success criteria.
2) Request SRE to enable mirror manifest with run_id and sample_rate.
3) Confirm telemetry tags are present in the mirror stream.
4) Validate that baseline and candidate endpoints are reachable.
5) Monitor dashboards (per-cohort) for first 6 hours. If any hard fails occur, follow hard-fail incident checklist.

Promotions, Canary Integration and Rollout Path:
- If all cohorts pass: promote candidate to canary (5–10% production, canary duration 48–96 hours) with continuous cohort monitoring.
- If a small number of low-impact cohorts fail: consider targeted mitigations (prompt templates, per-route fallback) and rerun shadow validation.

Appendix A — Example Shadow Routing YAML:
```yaml
shadow_run_id: cohort-shadow-2025-09
mirror_rules:
  - route: /v1/generate
    sample_rate: 0.1
    cohorts: [high-long-context-english, enterprise-integration-route]
candidate_endpoint: https://shadow-candidate.internal:8443/generate
baseline_endpoint: https://prod-model.internal:8443/generate
storage: s3://redwood-shadow-archive/cohort-shadow-2025-09/
```

Appendix B — Example cohort SQL (for data-team):
```
SELECT request_id, customer_id, route, token_count, language, timestamp
FROM request_logs
WHERE token_count > 2048 AND language = 'en' AND timestamp BETWEEN '{{start}}' AND '{{end}}';
```

Appendix C — CLI snippets:
- Start run: redwood-shadow run start --id cohort-shadow-2025-09 --manifest ./shadow.yaml
- Increase sampling for cohort: redwood-shadow run update --id cohort-shadow-2025-09 --cohort high-long-context-english --sample-rate 0.5
- Archive results: redwood-shadow artifacts bundle --id cohort-shadow-2025-09 --out ./artifacts.tar.gz

Troubleshooting common issues:
- Low sample counts: increase sample_rate for affected cohorts, extend window, or create synthetic probe generator limited to the target cohort patterns.
- High resource usage on candidate host: coordinate with SRE to throttle mirror throughput or scale candidate pool; prioritize critical cohorts.
- Inconsistent telemetry tags: stop the run, patch instrumentation, and restart to ensure validity of per-cohort aggregates.

Audit and Reporting:
- Every shadow run must attach an artifact containing anonymized examples (<=100 per failed cohort), a per-cohort metric CSV, and the approval decision.
- Maintain a run index (spreadsheet or internal DB) with run_id, start/end times, outcome, and link to artifacts for 12 months.

Notes and rationale:
- Cohort-driven validation focuses our signal-to-noise on high-value slices rather than aggregate metrics that can mask regressions. Adaptive sampling reduces cost while enabling focused amplification where it matters. Statistical gates balance sensitivity and false positive rates to avoid unnecessary rollbacks.

End of playbook.

Title: Adaptive Shadow Validation for Cold-Start and Telemetry-driven Promotion

Adaptive Shadow Validation for Cold-Start and Telemetry-driven Promotion

A practical playbook and validation contract for onboarding new model variants using adaptive shadow traffic to surface cold-start behaviors and telemetry-driven gating rules prior to canary or full promotion.
Shadow deployments are a core part of Redwood's model onboarding: they let us validate quality and infrastructure behavior without impacting production responses. Standard shadow runs often miss cold-start spike modes (first request to warmed kernels, kv-cache warmup) and do not adapt telemetry thresholds based on observed variance. This document specifies an adaptive shadow validation framework designed to detect cold-start failure modes, capture fine-grained telemetry, and produce deterministic promotion decisions.
Two recurring issues were observed in previous onboardings: (1) models that passed synthetic offline tests but regressed under realistic cold-start traffic patterns, and (2) static pass/fail thresholds that either blocked safe releases or allowed regressions when workload variance increased. The adaptive approach reduces false positives and false negatives by using staged sample budgets, variance-aware thresholds, and a telemetry-driven decision contract.
Applies to hosted and dedicated model promotions where the model affects real-time text generation or chat endpoints. This playbook is intended for ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SREs, and release managers. Not intended for embeddings-only shadowing (use embedding-specific onboarding checklist instead).
Use this playbook when: 1) adding a new model family or quantization profile, 2) changing kernel/backing runtime (CUDA->ROCm, new tensor cores), 3) onboarding models into Dedicated or Private with customer workload mirroring, or 4) promoting models that will handle low-latency interactive traffic.
- Baseline production telemetry (last 7 days) exported to the eval harness.
- A reproducible shadow routing configuration (mesh fork or 1% mirror is acceptable).
- An eval keypair and shadow dataset representing cold-start heavy queries (see sample generator below).
- Owners assigned: ML lead, Runtime owner, Release manager, SRE contact.
Collect the following telemetry at 1s granularity during shadow runs:
- request_id, timestamp, route, model_variant, region, backend_node
- latency p50/p90/p95/p99 (in ms)
- first-token-latency (ms)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (per-session)
- token_throughput (tokens/sec)
- GPU_utilization and memory_usage (per-host)
- error_rate (4xx/5xx) and internal_inference_errors
- output_quality metrics: sample-wise BLEU/ROUGE for structured tasks, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) or response-stability-index for chat
- feature_flags active
- seed/temperature and prompt-shard id
Adaptive validation uses a three-stage contract:
1) Warmup sanity (10-100 warmed sessions): verify no internal_inference_errors and kv_cache_hit_rate >= baseline * 0.85.
2) Cold-start probe (50-500 cold sessions): measure first-token-latency delta vs production baseline; require median delta <= 1.5x and p95 delta <= 2.0x unless compensated by model-quality improvements documented.
3) Stability window (synthetic mirror of 24h sample or 100K tokens): ensure rolling p95 latency within cost-latency budget and quality regressions <= 1% absolute on prioritized slices.
Thresholds are variance-aware: if sample variance > historical variance * 1.5, expand the confidence interval and require an additional verification stage before blocking promotion.
1) Create a shadow config: define routing percentage, mirror mode (fork vs linear replay), and cold-session fraction. Example YAML in 'sample_config'.
2) Generate shadow dataset: include a 25% cold-session fraction by inserting new session ids that have empty kv cache. Use the provided generator script.
3) Start a 2-hour warmup run with a 1% mirror for infrastructure checks. Collect telemetry and verify warmup sanity.
4) Run the cold-start probe for N=200 cold sessions distributed across regions and instance types. Evaluate first-token-latency deltas and kv cache behavior.
5) If probe passes, run the 24h stability window (or equivalent token-budget run) with full telemetry; compute rolling metrics and slice-aware quality checks.
6) Apply adaptive threshold rules: if variance triggers expansion, schedule a targeted rerun on impacted slices (e.g., long-context, high-temperature generations).
7) Produce a validation report (automated notebook) including per-slice histograms, variance tests (Levene), and a promotion recommendation: promote / require follow-up / block.
8) Sign-off: ML lead and Runtime owner must sign the report before canary promotion.

# shadow-run-config.yaml
mirror_mode: fork
routing_percentage: 1
cold_session_fraction: 0.25
budget_tokens: 100000
regions: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
instance_selector: {gpu_family: a100, min_mem_gb: 40}
telemetry_level: full
quality_checks:
  - name: semantic-similarity
    threshold: 0.92
    slices: [billing-qa, account-reset, long-context]
  - name: response-stability-index
    threshold: 0.98
# Start a shadow mirror (CLI)
redwood infra shadow start --config shadow-run-config.yaml --note "adaptive-shadow-jan2026"

# Example Python snippet to compute first-token-latency delta
import pandas as pd
prod = pd.read_parquet('prod_baseline.parquet')
shadow = pd.read_parquet('shadow_run.parquet')
merged = shadow.merge(prod, on=['route','slice'], suffixes=("_shadow","_prod"))
merged['first_token_delta'] = (merged['first_token_latency_shadow'] - merged['first_token_latency_prod']) / merged['first_token_latency_prod']
summary = merged.groupby('slice')['first_token_delta'].agg(['median','quantile'])
print(summary)
Reports must include: 1) per-slice metric tables (median, p95, variance), 2) histograms for first-token-latency comparing shadow vs prod, 3) kv-cache warmup curves (kv_cache_hit_rate over session steps), 4) per-node GPU telemetry overlay, and 5) a short executive summary with recommendation. Upload the report to the eval dashboard and link the job id in the release ticket.
Primary SLOs for promotion decision:
- first-token-latency median delta <= 1.5x and p95 delta <= 2.0x
- rolling latency p95 must remain within absolute budget: p95 <= 350ms for interactive routes, <= 800ms for long-batch routes
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop <= 15% relative to baseline
- production-critical slice quality regressions <= 1% absolute
- infra error_rate <= 0.01%
If any primary SLO is violated, promotion is blocked unless compensated and documented in the report.
If sample variance for any primary metric exceeds historical variance * 1.5, the harness will: 1) auto-extend the run by 2x sample budget, 2) trigger a rerun on the impacted slices with focused sampling, and 3) notify owners via PagerDuty (runtime-owner escalation). If after reruns the metric remains outside thresholds, create a regression-triage ticket and schedule a 2-day investigation window before any manual override.
If promoted model causes production regressions identified in the first 24 hours (p95 latency increase > 10% absolute or slice-quality regression > 2% absolute), immediately activate rollback: set routing to previous model variant and open an incident with 'model-promotion-regression' tag. Postmortem must include shadow logs, probe artifacts, and a root-cause analysis within 7 days.
ML lead: Marcus Bell (ml@redwood.ai)
Runtime owner: Elena Park (runtime@redwood.ai)
SRE oncall: see oncall rota (link)
Release manager: Jorge Ramirez (releases@redwood.ai)
A small generator is provided to synthesize cold sessions and long-tail prompts. Usage:
python tools/generate_shadow_dataset.py --size 20000 --cold_fraction 0.25 --slices 'billing-qa,long-context,signup'
Generator creates: shadow_prompts.jsonl, session_ids.csv, slice_metadata.csv
Links and artifacts to attach to the promotion ticket: 1) shadow job id, 2) eval notebook URL, 3) sample_config YAML, 4) telemetry parquet exports, 5) sign-off checklist (signed PDFs)
Integrate the adaptive shadow validation contract into the automated promotion pipeline: - implement automatic variance checks in the eval harness, - add a UI widget in the eval dashboard that surfaces cold-start histograms, - schedule a roadshow with platform teams to adopt the contract for Dedicated onboarding.
This playbook intentionally biases toward conservative promotion decisions for low-latency interactive routes. Teams may adjust thresholds for batch-only workloads after coordinating with Runtime owners.

Add tiered batching dashboards (latency/queue/batch size) with cardinality-safe dimensions

Title: Vector shape / compatibility issue causing sudden rerank ordering regressions after embedding model swap

Vector shape / compatibility issue causing sudden rerank ordering regressions after embedding model swap

Customer reports that after switching their embedding model from open-embed-v2-512 -> open-embed-v3-384 in their Dedicated pool, reranker results for several search flows degraded: top-N ordering changed unpredictably and relevance dropped. Some rerank requests return quickly but with low-quality ordering; others show higher latency and occasional 500s. Customer switched models to save cost and saw immediate impact in production traffic.
1) In customer account (Acme Payments) with dedicated pool in eu-west, change embedding model to open-embed-v3-384 and leave reranker pinned to open-rerank-512. 2) Run batch of 1000 search+rerank calls against route /v1/rerank using stored corpus. 3) Compare top-5 ordering and relevance metrics to baseline (embeddings=512). 4) Observe increased mismatches and occasional 500 errors with traces pointing to reranker-service.
- Top-N ordering degraded for 12% of queries by manual eval sets.
- Some requests have 500 errors with stack traces referencing 'vector_dot_product: length mismatch'.
- Median tail latency for rerank increased from 110ms -> 420ms for affected route.
- Customer sees billing unchanged but perceived quality regression.
- Backwards-compatible behavior where swapping to a different embedding model should either be blocked if dimensionality incompatible with pinned reranker, or auto-converted/handled without quality regressions.
- No 500s due to vector length mismatches.
- Latency should not spike by >2x for same traffic pattern.
Initial triage: traces show the reranker operator assumes 512-d vectors and performs native dot-product kernel on GPU. When 384-d vectors arrive, there is an internal validation error in native kernel that surfaces as 500. We also observed a compatibility shim in Dedicated cluster that attempts to pad/truncate vectors on the CPU for 'compatibility' and that path is single-threaded causing latency spikes. Hypotheses: 1) Model metadata for open-embed-v3-384 didn't register dimensionality with routing layer so reranker was not alerted. 2) Compatibility conversion code path is causing both quality degradation (zero padding changes vector semantics) and latency due to CPU-bound conversions. 3) Some edge requests bypass the shim and hit GPU kernel causing length-mismatch 500s.
