Title: Local GPU driver/CUDA troubleshooting breadcrumbs

Local GPU driver/CUDA troubleshooting breadcrumbs

Quick personal breadcrumbs for the sequence of steps I tried while debugging the laptop / local docker GPU failures. This is messy — notes to self and hypotheses.

Date range: 2024-04-10 -> 2024-06-12
Machine: personal dev laptop (lenovo thinkpad + external eGPU) / local workstation
GPU: RTX 3080 (10GB) — sometimes shows as 10026MiB total in nvidia-smi, sometimes 10240 depending on driver.
Driver + Toolkit situation seen while debugging:
  - Host driver: 535.XX (apt package from graphics-drivers PPA)
  - CUDA toolkit installed in /usr/local/cuda-11.8 and also /usr/local/cuda-12.1 (leftover)
  - Conda envs with cudatoolkit=11.8 and 12.0 tried
  - PyTorch wheel in env: torch==2.1.0 (built for CUDA 11.8)

Symptoms / errors observed (copied raw as I saw them):
  - RuntimeError: CUDA error: driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
    (seen launching python train_small.py inside container built FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1-base)

  - ImportError: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
    (happened in container when nvidia-container-toolkit not configured correctly)

  - CudaRuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version (torch.cuda.init())

  - OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4.00 GiB (GPU 0; 10.00 GiB total capacity; 6.12 GiB already allocated; 2.00 GiB free; 8.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
    -> This happened even when batch_size=1 on an intentionally tiny model (2-layer mlp), so suspect memory leak or pinned-memory/worker DataLoader issue.

Commands I ran (and outputs I inspected):
  - nvidia-smi -L             # lists GPUs, model ids
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
    -> driver shows 535.54, mem 10192 MiB
  - nvcc --version            # only present when cuda toolkit in PATH
  - python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.backends.cudnn.version())"
    -> False / '11.8' / 8400 (varied between runs)

Container repro attempts:
  - docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi  # works on host: shows GPUs inside container
  - docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
    -> False (torch build mismatch: wheel expecting 11.8)
  - Verified nvidia-container-runtime and nvidia-container-toolkit installed and daemon restarted.

Host-level investigations:
  - ldd /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep cuda
    -> pointed to /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 and also had unresolved references when toolkit 12 present on PATH
  - ls -l /usr/local | grep cuda
    -> cuda -> cuda-12.1 (symlinked) but conda env had 11.8 libs -> classic mismatch.
  - echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH # sometime empty, sometimes set by .bashrc to /usr/local/cuda/lib64

Memory/OOM-specific debugging I tried:
  - python snippet to monitor memory:
    import torch, time
    for i in range(10):
      x = torch.randn(32, 1024, device='cuda')
      print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated()/1024**2, torch.cuda.memory_reserved()/1024**2)
      time.sleep(0.5)
    -> observed memory_reserved increasing even after del x; required torch.cuda.empty_cache(); suspected caching + leak in training loop.

  - Reproduced OOM with DataLoader pin_memory=True + num_workers>0: memory spikes immediately at first batch when num_workers=4. Suspect worker processes allocate pinned buffers.
  - Workaround: set pin_memory=False or num_workers=0. That reduces immediate spike.

Driver / runtime mismatch attempts and notes:
  - Hypothesis A: Host driver (535.x) supports CUDA 12.x, but PyTorch wheel built for CUDA 11.8 — should still work because driver is backwards compatible usually. However, containers and PATH pointing to 12.1 toolkit cause ldconfig/ldd to pick wrong libcuda at runtime -> mismatch error.
  - Hypothesis B: There are leftover files from system CUDA installs in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu that shadow conda libs.
  - Hypothesis C: nvidia-container-toolkit not mounting libcuda in some container variants, resulting in 'libcuda.so.1 missing' inside container. Verified with 'docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base ls -l /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 | head'

What I tried to fix (and result):
  - Reinstalled NVIDIA driver (apt purge -> add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers -> apt install nvidia-driver-535)
    -> After reboot, host nvidia-smi ok. Did not fix container torch import errors.
  - Remove /usr/local/cuda-12.1 symlink, point /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-11.8 (temporary)
    -> python in host env now shows torch.cuda.is_available() = True in some envs. But containers built from 12.1 base still fail.
  - Rebuilt local docker image FROM nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime, installed pip wheel for torch 2.1 (CUDA 11.8) -> fixed torch.cuda.is_available() inside container.
  - For the OOM case: set DataLoader(pin_memory=False), num_workers=0 -> run succeeded under low batch size.

Logs / dmesg extracts I kept:
  - Apr 12 10:13:44 laptop kernel: [12345.678901] Out of memory: Killed process 3261 (python) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:987654kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
  - Apr 12 10:13:44 laptop kernel: [12345.679012] python invoked oom-killer: gfp-mask=0x20d2ca, order=0, oom_score_adj=0
  -> This indicates severe host memory pressure (not necessarily GPU-only). Need to check swap usage and system memory pressure when dataloader workers spawn pinned buffers.

Open questions / TODO (prioritized):
  1) Investigate whether DataLoader pinned-memory allocation is leaking on this kernel/driver combo. Steps: reproduce with small script that spawns workers and repeatedly creates pin_memory tensors. Collect /proc/<pid>/smaps and /proc/<pid>/status to see locked memory.
  2) Add test that runs inside nvidia/cuda:11.8 vs 12.1 images to reproduce lib mismatch -> create minimal Dockerfile and upload to GH issue.
  3) Try switching to conda-installed cudatoolkit=11.8 (instead of system /usr/local/cuda) and ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH empty to force conda libs used. Document steps that reliably fixed it for me.
  4) Check with SRE/infra if graphics-driver PPA upgrade is allowed on workstation fleet: we may need driver pinned across dev fleet.

Workaround notes (what I keep using locally):
  - For containers: base images must match PyTorch wheel CUDA version (11.8 wheels -> use nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime).
  - For quick tests: conda create -n torch11 python=3.10 pytorch==2.1 torchvision cudatoolkit=11.8 -c pytorch -c conda-forge -> seems consistent.
  - For OOM: set pin_memory=False on DataLoader and reduce num_workers to 0 if on laptop. On CI / Dedicated machines with large RAM, pin_memory can be enabled.

Notes to self (less formal):
  - Keep docker images labelled clearly with CUDA version in README -> stops confusion.
  - When hitting driver/runtime mismatch -> always check ldd on the torch cuda libs and nvidia-smi inside container.
  - If you see 'driver version is insufficient', try reboot after driver reinstall (old driver still loaded).
  - If libcuda missing in container: ensure --gpus all passed and nvidia-container-toolkit installed.

Snippets to paste into issues / troubleshooting template: (copy-paste friendly)
  - nvidia-smi output:
    +---------------------------------+
    | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.1 |
    +---------------------------------+
  - Python checks:
    python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"

  - Quick repro script for DataLoader spike:
    import torch, time
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset

    class Dummy(Dataset):
        def __len__(self): return 100000
        def __getitem__(self, i): return torch.randn(1024), 0
\    loader = DataLoader(Dummy(), batch_size=1, num_workers=4, pin_memory=True)
    for i, (x,y) in enumerate(loader):
        if i%10==0:
            print(i, torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0)/1024**2, torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0)/1024**2)
        if i>100: break

    -> observe large jump on first worker spawn.

Final short summary:
  - Primary root causes seen: mismatched container base CUDA vs PyTorch wheel; host /usr/local/cuda symlink pointing to different toolkit; DataLoader pinned memory causing host RAM pressure and apparent OOMs.
  - Short-term fixes: align container CUDA version to wheel, use conda cudatoolkit for dev envs, disable pin_memory / reduce num_workers on laptop.

If I make this reproducible I'll attach a minimal Dockerfile + script and open GH issue (INF-312)

-- Ava

Title: GPU OOM tactic logbook

GPU OOM tactic logbook

Purpose:
Quick personal log for reproducible checks and fast heuristics when hitting intermittent GPU OOMs that seem correlated with driver/runtime/library mismatches. This is a running scratchpad — commands tried, raw snippets, hypotheses, and next steps. Not for public circulation until cleaned up.

Summary of incident pattern observed: 
- Worker pods on Dedicated cluster occasionally OOM during long generation jobs.
- Symptoms: process dies with CUDA OOM but nvidia-smi shows plenty of free memory across time; NVML reports transient error codes.
- Suspected: library mix (host libcuda + container libcudart mismatch), delayed kernel eviction, and sporadic vram fragmentation caused by small allocations + TRT engine builds.

Repro quick-checks (commands to run on affected host / container):
1) Host driver + runtime versions
   sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || true
   nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version,name,memory.total,memory.free --format=csv
   # sample output (captured 2026-02-19):
   # NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86.05    CUDA Version: 12.1
   # GPU-0, A100-SXM4, 40960 MiB, 38720 MiB free

2) Inside container: runtime / linked libs\   
   python -c "import torch,sys; print('torch',torch.__version__); print('cuda',torch.version.cuda); print('cuda_available',torch.cuda.is_available())"
   python -m pip show tensorrt || true
   LD_DEBUG=libs python -c 'import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1")' 2>&1 | sed -n '1,80p'
   ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cuda || true

   # observed: container reports CUDA runtime 11.8 (packaged), host driver 535 (runtime 12.x) — mismatch but generally okay; however LD_DEBUG shows libcuda being resolved from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 on the host rather than the expected vendor path in the container.

3) Small repro that sometimes triggers immediate OOM (useful for confirming allocation behavior):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python - <<'PY'
   import torch
   print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
   a = [torch.empty((1024,1024,256), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda') for _ in range(8)]
   print('allocated', sum(x.element_size()*x.nelement() for x in a))
   torch.cuda.synchronize()
   PY

   # On good hosts this completes; on bad ones it crashes with:
   # RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 39.10 GiB already allocated; 128.00 MiB free; 1.90 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

4) NVML / dmesg traces when failure happens:
   dmesg | grep -i -E "NVRM|gpu|OOM|nvml" -n | tail -n 80
   journalctl -k -o short-iso | grep -E "NVRM|nvidia" -n | tail -n 80

   # sample dmesg lines captured:
   # [ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x11: NVRM_INF_DRIVER_NOT_LOADED)
   # [ 1240.234567] nvlink: Nvlink timeout on fw handshake

   # NVML log snippet when probed programmatically:
   # NVML: Driver/library version mismatch (expected 535, found 525)

Commands/tricks already tried on this host (and their effects):
- Restarting nvidia-persistenced and container runtime (systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced docker) — sometimes temporarily clears the failure, but it returns under load.
- nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0 — only available on compute-locked GPUs; returned "GPU in use" on our cluster so ineffective.
- Killing user processes owning large allocations (nvidia-smi pmon) — immediate memory reclamation observed; but the underlying process crashes cause customer-visible errors.
- Removing LD_PRELOAD from startup scripts where we previously injected a profiling shim — after removal, incidence dropped by ~30% in one pod type.

Hypotheses (ordered by current confidence):
1) Mixed libcuda/driver versions: containers include prebuilt CUDA artifacts (cudart/cuBLAS) that bind to a host libcuda of a different SONAME, producing odd NVML errors and intermittent allocation failures. Observation: LD_DEBUG showed host libcuda being used despite container expecting a different ABI.
2) Per-process fragmentation: repeated small allocations and TRT engine builds cause fragmentation in driver-side device allocator, leading to large alloc failure despite aggregated free memory reported by nvidia-smi.

Title: diagnostic-oom-driver-hypotheses-scratch

diagnostic-oom-driver-hypotheses-scratch

Quick scratchpad — do not treat as final. Goal: capture commands, error snippets, timelines, and hypotheses for recurring OOM-like crashes on k8s nodes (p5/gp102) when running batched inference with kv-cache warming. Context: intermittent crashes over last 2 weeks, suspects: driver/libcuda ABI drift, mixed libcuda/libnvidia-open, and kernel upgrade timing.

Summary of observed symptoms:
- Process exits with CUDA OOM (RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory) but NVML reports free memory > model allocation immediately after crash.
- dmesg shows 'oom-killer' touching unrelated process or no oom-killer entry depending on node.
- Container logs include: "failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes on device 0: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" followed by rapid restart loop.
- Sometimes we also see: "undefined symbol: cuInit" or ld.so complaining about libcuda.so.1: wrong ELF class or version mismatch.
- Reproduced locally once on node with mixed driver packages (nvidia-driver-535 + libcuda from 540 staging) — reproducible with simple memtest script below.

Commands I ran and outputs (trimmed):
1) nvidia-smi -a
Timestamp                       : Mon Feb 28 12:17:03 2026
Driver Version                  : 535.98
CUDA Version                    : 12.2
Attached GPUs                   : 1
FB Memory Usage                 : 12012MiB / 24268MiB
Processes: ID, Type, GPU Memory
  2345      C+G    11000MiB  (inference process)

2) python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))'
'11.8'  <-- mismatch: runtime reports torch built against CUDA 11.8 but system CUDA is 12.2

3) ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 14 Jan 15  /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.1
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root  6.2M Jan 15 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1  <-- file present (from driver 535 package)

4) readelf -sW /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuInit
  102: 000000000002f8b0   34 FUNC    GLOBAL DEFAULT   16 cuInit@GLIBC_PRIVATE

5) Docker container logs snippet:
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total capacity; 20.90 GiB already allocated; 3.10 GiB free)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
OSError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Interpretation: mixed signs — PyTorch complaining about memory, then post-failure the runtime tries to call into a different CUDA runtime library and fails to load it. Suggests that at crash time the process may be in an inconsistent state where some addresses are mapped to different GLIBC_PRIVATE sym versions.

Minimal repro (local) - mem_hammer.py:
# allocate large tensors in loop and touch kv cache sim
import torch, time
for i in range(200):
    a = torch.empty((1024,1024,32), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda')
    a.normal_()
    time.sleep(0.05)
    if i % 10 == 0:
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

On a node with driver+lib mismatch this leads to: kernel panic in nvidia_uvm or silent process exit.

Other logs of interest:
- dmesg tail after one crash: 
[Feb28 12:18:07] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (error=3)
[Feb28 12:18:07] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU is lost
[Feb28 12:18:07] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13, pid=2345, GPU has fallen off the bus

- journalctl for container runtime: 
Mar 01 03:34:01 node-17 dockerd[2890]: time="2026-03-01T03:34:01Z" level=error msg="failed to start container: driver failed programming external connectivity on endpoint..."

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Library/driver ABI mismatch: userspace sees libcuda.so from one driver version but kernel module/version expects another -> NVML reports inconsistent state, some functions missing (cuInit symbol issues). Explains 'cuInit' and libcuda version errors.
2) UVM kernel module crashes under specific allocation patterns (large contiguous pinned pages), causing the kernel to mark GPU lost and subsequent user processes get weird OOM or symbol errors when runtime tries to reinit.
3) Namespace/sandboxing mismatch: container image vendors different glibc/CUDA runtime (conda + cudatoolkit) vs host drivers -> at process restart time loader picks host libs or container overlay libs unpredictably.
4) Race between driver update and container restarts: nodes that had driver package upgraded but not rebooted show intermittent behavior.

What I tried (and results):
- Reinstalling driver 535 on affected node -> briefly stable, then reproduction within hours when we run larger batch sizes.
- Pinning torch to cuda11.8 build version in container image -> reduced frequency but did not eliminate (suggests partial mitigation).
- Forced module reload (modprobe -r nvidia_uvm; modprobe nvidia_uvm) -> when successful, GPU comes back; if module unload fails, node needs reboot.
- Running small reproducer under nsjail / pivot_root -> same fail mode, so not purely k8s kubelet/CRI-specific.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Add a short e2e job that repeatedly runs mem_hammer.py on a staging p5 fleet with driver version matrix (532, 535, 540) to capture kernel logs and nvdec dumps. Capture kdump if available.
- Add LD_DEBUG=libs and ldd python binary output to our crash wrapper to capture which libcuda/libcudart are being resolved at launch vs at crash time.
- Create a short kube daemonset that periodically attempts modprobe -r nvidia_uvm and logs success/failure: this will tell us if module unload races exist.
- Open a tracking ticket (JIRA-ENG-4123) with kernel dmesg, NVML traces, and representative container images.

Longer-term ideas:
- Harden container runtime: pre-load and RTLD_DEEPBIND libcuda from host during startup so userland cannot mask it with conda's cudatoolkit. Test for regressions.
- Work with driver vendor to get a backtrace from uvm when crash occurs (requires repro and kdump).

Title: Driver shim tangle debug diary

Driver shim tangle debug diary

Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad tracking an intermittent GPU OOM / library mismatch that looks like a driver/libcuda shim problem. Notes are noisy — chronological breadcrumbs, commands tried, and hypotheses for a later clean write-up.

Summary of issue:
- Host machines sometimes OOM during model init (large KV cache allocation), but only in certain containers/pods.
- Error surface varies: sometimes CUDA reports an illegal memory access, sometimes the app crashes with dlopen errors about libcuda.so.1, other times nvml init fails in Python with exception "Failed to initialize NVML: unknown error".
- Reproducible on one dev node (gpu-node-17) and sometimes on a cluster worker after a driver upgrade window.

Environment snapshot (mixed):
- Host kernel: 6.1.23-rt (custom)
- Host NVIDIA driver: 525.85.12 (dkms-built module, /proc/driver/nvidia/version shows 525.85.12)
- Container base images observed: nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu20.04, cuda:12.2-runtime-ubuntu22.04, and smaller slim python images with wheel-installed torch.
- Conda envs + pip wheels for torch compiled against CUDA 11.7/11.8 in many cases.
- Some nodes have both /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host driver-provided) and container-bundled libcuda in /usr/local/cuda/lib64 (occasionally).

Commands & outputs (snippets taken during repro attempts):
1) Check driver on host:
$ cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 525.85.12 Wed Dec 28 10:15:47 UTC 2025

$ nvidia-smi
Thu Mar 12 12:11:04 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

2) Inside container (problematic run):
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
11.8
True

But then run crashes when allocating a 30GB buffer:
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 31.5 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total capacity; 46.3 GiB already allocated; 1.25 GiB free; 2.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

3) Docker inspect and mount situation:
- Container launched with --gpus all and volume mounts: /usr/local/cuda -> host /usr/local/cuda-12.2 (some nodes)
- Other runs use NVIDIA container toolkit enabling host libcuda visibility.

4) ldd of _C.so (torch CUDA extension) inside container:
$ ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f0e...)
  libcudart.so.11.0 => not found
  libcusparse.so.11 => not found
(-> indicates mixed library visibility; loader falls back to host libcuda but missing full cuda toolkit libs)

5) ldconfig cache vs LD_LIBRARY_PATH:
- Container ldconfig shows host-provided libcuda in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, but container's /usr/local/cuda/lib64 has cuda 12.2 libs. If LD_LIBRARY_PATH points at /usr/local/cuda/lib64, sometimes the app picks up inconsistent symbols (abi mismatch).

6) Example dlopen error seen in production crashlog:
python: symbol lookup error: /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so: undefined symbol: cuGetErrorName
(typical when libcuda provides older/newer symbol set than the runtime expects)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Shim/mismatched libcuda on loader path: container picks host libcuda by SONAME but other CUDA toolkit libs are from a different version -> symbol mismatch and subtle behavior like malloc not failing properly -> OOMs or illegal accesses.
2) Partial driver upgrade state on some nodes: kernel module updated but userland libs cached in container image layers (docker image built earlier referencing old /usr/local/cuda), causing two versions to be seen at runtime.
3) LD_PRELOAD or site-specific LD_LIBRARY_PATH in launch scripts (we saw /opt/nvidia/lib in one init script) forcing wrong ordering.
4) NVML init sometimes fails because pci device node appears/vanishes during driver module reloads or nvidia-fabric manager restarts; app interprets that as OOM and falls back badly.

Commands I tried to validate hypotheses (notes + results):
- Ran modinfo nvidia on host, compared vermagic vs module in /lib/modules. All matched on node-17.
- Reproduced container with both /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 and /usr/local/cuda/lib64 present and toggled LD_LIBRARY_PATH:
  * With LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu -> torch crashes with undefined symbol.
  * With LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -> torch init succeeds but later OOM behavior not consistent.
- ldd tree for Python extension pointed to mixed versions; forcing LD_LIBRARY_PATH to host lib path made symbols resolve but revealed other missing toolkit libs (cusparse, cublas).
- Tried LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> different segfault (illegal instruction) in fast math kernel (likely ABI mismatch).

Interim mitigation tested:
- Added explicit container startup step to run: "update-alternatives --set cuda /usr/local/cuda-12.2" and export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64 then restart process. This made one failing job succeed (likely because it forced consistent toolkit+runtime).
- For pods that use host mounts for /usr/local/cuda, changed to rely on host drivers only (no container-bundled libcuda) — reduced incidence but not eliminated.

Observations / oddities:
- On some nodes torch reports CUDA 11.x in python even though host nvidia-smi shows CUDA 12.2. That indicates torch was built against 11.x and is finding a compatibility shim.
- Some crash logs show NVML error before memory allocation attempts — suggests driver/userland desync can fail NVML and still allow some CUDA ops, causing inconsistent free memory accounting.
- When the node had ongoing driver updates (post-deploy), restoration via system reboot temporarily fixed the issue for a day.

Next steps (practical plan):
1) Repro script: minimal docker image that purposely contains mismatched libcuda in /usr/local/cuda and host libcuda in /usr/lib, run a short torch program that allocates and frees a bunch of buffers to trigger OOM/illegal access. Goal: produce minimal repro and deterministic crash.
2) Run full binary check: compare SONAMEs and symbol tables (nm -D) of libcuda on host vs container. Capture differences in symbols used by libc10_cuda.so.
3) Coordinate with infra to pin node-17 to a single driver/toolkit stack for testing (either host + container consistent 12.2 or fully rely on host libs and remove container cuda libs).
4) Add container startup validation: run a small script to verify that ldd for critical .so resolves to a consistent directory (all libs from same cuda version). If mismatch, fail fast and emit helpful logs.
5) Add automated check in CI that builds images and runs ldd on torch libs to detect potential multi-version exposure.

Notes / links for later:
- Slack thread: #infra-gpu (referenced messages around Mar 11-12)
- Ticket: JIRA-INF-1872 (driver upgrade window)
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (runtime container changes)

Random crumbs I wrote while debugging:
- Check /etc/ld.so.conf.d for stale cuda paths that survived image layering.
- If using NVIDIA container toolkit, ensure nvidia-container-runtime-hook isn't injecting old paths.
- Watch for docker build ARGs that bake /usr/local/cuda symlink into image against older host during ephemeral build runner.
- Consider enabling device-level healthcheck in k8s to detect NVML failures and automatically recycle pod.

Conclusion (temporary):
Most evidence points to loader-level mixed-version exposure (host libcuda vs container toolkit libs) producing ABI/behavior inconsistencies. Short-term: add startup ldd checks + enforce single toolkit version in images; long-term: improve infra driver rollout process and add automated ldd-based gating for container images that include CUDA libs.

- 2026-03-12 11:00: temporary mitigation applied on staging, reduced failures

Title: driver-shim-oom-audit-scratchpad

driver-shim-oom-audit-scratchpad

Purpose: scratchpad for a recurring intermittent OOM / cuInit / libcuda mismatch we've seen on a subset of prod GPU nodes. Goal is to capture commands tried, exact error snippets, quick hypotheses, and minimal repro notes so SRE/infra can triage fast.

Background / symptom summary:
- Multiple tasks (chat model shards, refactor branch) have been failing with either immediate CUDA init errors inside containers or throwing OOMs mid-generation with inconsistent reported VRAM usage.
- Failures are clustered to nodes in rack-3 (nvidia-driver 535.86) and a new kpatch rolled out 2026-02-26.
- Containers built on host A (driver 535) sometimes fail when scheduled onto host B (driver 530) with the same image.

Representative error snippets (copied raw):
1) container startup / cuda init:
   2026-03-05T09:14:33Z ERROR runtime: cuInit(0) failed: unknown error
   runtime: failed to initialize CUDA driver: cuInit returned 999

2) undefined symbol on load:
   python: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: undefined symbol: cuDeviceGetAttribute

3) OOM during generation (trainer process):
   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 12.4 GiB already allocated; 1.80 GiB free; 1.16 GiB cached)
   NOTE: free/allocated numbers from pytorch don't always reflect nvml output.

4) NVML mismatch in dmesg:
   [ 1234.567890] NVRM: API mismatch: the client has the 535.86 and the kernel module has 530.41

Commands & quick probes tried (in order):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION -- showed different driver versions reported inside container vs host on failure nodes.
- docker run --rm --gpus all --env NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility --entrypoint bash IMAGE -c "ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* && strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | head"
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; import os; print(torch._C.__file__)') to check linked libcuda path. Found libcuda symlink pointing to host-provided lib but versions mismatched.
- ldconfig -p | grep libcuda to inspect system cache. On one node ld.so.cache had stale 530 references.
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version and modinfo nvidia to compare kernel module version.
- dmesg | grep NVRM to surface API mismatch messages (see above).
- strace -f -e open,openat -p <pid> on model process during startup to see what lib paths are opened. Observed mixed /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and /usr/local/cuda/compat links.
- python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')" to provoke symbol lookup errors; reproduced the undefined symbol message when host lib and container runtime were misaligned.

Container / image notes:
- Images are multi-stage, base image includes cuda-toolkit-11.8 (for build), runtime relies on host libcuda; we intentionally do not ship libcuda in image.
- Some developer images accidentally include /usr/local/cuda/lib64 symlink which masks host lib when running with some runtimes.
- Recent change: switched from nvidia-container-runtime v3 -> v4 in Feb; behavior differs when container includes partial CUDA libs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver / kernel module mismatch (API mismatch) after partial driver roll (most likely). dmesg explicitly shows API mismatch. Explanation: module on host still older (530) but userspace libraries updated to 535; result = undefined symbols or cuInit failure.
2) Image ships a partial CUDA userlib (e.g., libcuda.so stub) that gets picked up instead of host-provided library, causing missing symbols or version skew. (Seen in traces where /usr/local/cuda/lib64 present).
3) NVML/driver state corrupted on warm node after long uptime + repeated container loads; only full driver reload solves it.
4) Pytorch caching / fragmentation: allocations grow because of suboptimal caching when kernels differ causing different memory footprints; explains OOM-like numbers that don't match nvml. Less likely for startup cuInit errors.

Interventions attempted / results:
- Reboot node (temp fix): nodes rebooted & all tasks recovered for ~48h, then failures recurred. Suggests kernel module + userlib drift over updates.
- Full driver reinstall (535.86) on one problematic node: fixed immediately. Leaving this node as a canary.
- Forced removal of /usr/local/cuda/lib64 symlink from image and rebuild: some reduction in failures for that image variant.
- Replacing nvidia-container-runtime v4 -> v3 on a test host: inconsistent results; v3 picked host lib more reliably in one case.
- Added preflight check in task runner to run `ldd` on torch._C and ensure libcuda.so resolves to host path; we started failing fast (reject scheduling) if mismatch detected.

Minimal repro notes (how to reproduce locally):
1) Host A: install driver 535 (userspace libs) but don't update kernel module (simulate mismatch) -> modprobe shows 530 kernel module.
2) Build image that does NOT include libcuda but DOES include /usr/local/cuda/lib64 with some compatibility stubs.
3) Run docker with --gpus all and nvidia runtime v4; inside container run "python -c \"import torch; torch.zeros(1).cuda()\"" -> observe cuInit or undefined symbol.

Checklist for next triage run (whoever picks this up):
- [ ] Collect `modinfo nvidia`, `/proc/driver/nvidia/version`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` from host and from within a repro container.
- [ ] Gather `ldd` output of torch._C inside failing container and `readelf -d` on libcuda.so.1 if present.
- [ ] Check `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` and `ldconfig -v` for stale entries. Snapshot `ld.so.cache`.
- [ ] If dmesg shows API mismatch, escalate to infra to verify recent driver rollout plan and kernel module build status (kernel ABI drift).
- [ ] Try reproducing with singularity / podman to see runtime-specific path munging.
- [ ] Add small regression test: start a container that tries `ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')` and fail-fast if symbol lookup fails; hook into our scheduler pre-scheduling check.

Notes to self / messy other observations:
- Observed one case where `nvidia-smi` inside container reported driver 535 while `modinfo nvidia` on host reported 530 – weird but consistent with partial upgrade where userspace libs were updated but kernel module not yet recompiled.
- A workaround that sometimes helps: set LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 inside container (forces host lib) but it's brittle and not a long-term solution.
- There may be a subtle race with our node updater: it swaps driver rpm files, restarts kubelet, but doesn't always unload old kernel module in time.
- Look at salt/ansible playbook that did driver rollout on 2026-02-26; link: infra playbook PR 924.

Open questions:
- Why do some containers pick up host lib and others pick up image-supplied lib with same runtime? Is it ordering of lib paths vs LD_LIBRARY_PATH set by wrapper?
- Is there a chance that CUDA toolkit packages from apt pull a partial libcuda stub into the image at build time? Need to audit base images.

Immediate action plan (short):
- Add fast-fail preflight in runner to detect libcuda mismatch (already started).
- Schedule canary nodes to fully reinstall kernel module + driver and keep them observation-only for a week.
- Audit a sample of top 10 failing images to see if they ship any CUDA userlibs.
- Make a small doc for devs: "don’t include libcuda in images; if you must, pin fully compatible versions and test against host drivers".

If you pick this up, start by grabbing the node logs at /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and /var/log/dmesg* and ping me (Maya) in #infra-gpu with node name.

Purpose:
Quick personal sleuthing log for the strange OOM / driver mismatch I hit on the device-sandbox yesterday. Intended as a timeline + commands tried + micro-hypotheses so I can hand off to infra or pick up later. Not exhaustive.

Context / reproducibility:
- Host: ubuntu-22.04 (ec2 m6i-like dev nodes for local repro) with attached A100-40GB.
- Container base: nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-base-ubuntu22.04 -> but we also tried 11.8 variants.
- Framework: PyTorch nightly build pinned in container wheel. Repro is intermittent (fails after long warmup or under memory pressure).
- Symptoms: sudden CUDA OOM during KV cache growth (inference warmup). Sometimes container logs show libcuda link issues before OOM.

Observed errors (snippets copied from logs):
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.50 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 36.20 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 36.85 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- "libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory" (only on a few nodes)
- "cuda_driver: failed to initialize (UNKNOWN ERROR)"
- "E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:XXXX] failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN"
- "undefined symbol: cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain_v2" (appears when mixing 11.x runtime with 12.x libcuda)

Commands I ran (notes inline):
- nvidia-smi -> baseline GPU state and driver reported (Driver Version: 535.86, CUDA Version: 12.1)
- docker run --gpus all -it --rm --entrypoint bash nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-base-ubuntu22.04
  - inside container: ldconfig -p | grep libcuda  # check available libcuda symlinks
  - ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so | grep cuda  # see what libcudart is linked against
- dpkg -l | grep nvidia  # on host to check driver packaging
- ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda*  # confirm host libcuda presence and symlinks
- strace -f -e open,read -p <pid>  # attach during container start to see which lib path fails
- LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)"  # to show loader resolution in runtime

What I observed after runs:
- Containers using cuda:12.x images on hosts with older driver (e.g., 520.x) sometimes still work but hit subtle API mismatches when using new cuInit symbols.
- Some nodes had /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> libnvidia-ml.so symlink missing. Kernel updates had left stale .so files.
- When we preloaded host libcuda into the container with --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/host-lib:ro and LD_PRELOAD=/host-lib/libcuda.so.1 the workload either: a) worked around missing link, or b) hit symbol mismatch (undefined symbol). So preloading is brittle.

Micro-hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver vs runtime mismatch: host driver is older/newer than the container CUDA runtime, causing missing symbols (cuInit_v2 vs cuInit) or incompatible expectations.
2) Partial upgrades left mixed libcuda variants on host (multiple versions present) and container picks wrong one via ldconfig path order.
3) Memory fragmentation (kvcache + model buffers) + driver memory accounting differences between driver versions leads to OOM only on some driver versions.
4) PyTorch or runtime bug that surfaces only when certain driver returns unexpected free mem values (e.g., returns smaller free memory and triggers aggressive reservation).

Quick repro recipe (for infra to try):
1) On suspect node, run: docker run --gpus all -it --rm --entrypoint bash nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-base-ubuntu22.04
2) Inside: apt update && apt install -y psmisc strace lsof
3) pip install torch --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cpu  # or use our wheel in artifacts
4) Run small script that grows KV cache gradually (attached below) until OOM and capture dmesg + container logs.

Attached tiny test (paste into container as grow_kv.py):
-----
import torch
from time import sleep
T = torch.empty((1024,1024,512), device='cuda:0')  # allocate chuncks repeatedly to simulate warmup
chunks = []
try:
    for i in range(100):
        chunks.append(torch.empty((1024,256,256), device='cuda:0'))
        print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated(), torch.cuda.memory_reserved())
        sleep(0.5)
except Exception as e:
    print('fail', e)
-----

What not to do (lessons learned):
- Avoid LD_PRELOAD host libcuda unless you fully control driver/runtime versions — it trades one failure for symbol mismatch.
- Don't mix vendor driver packages with custom installed .so copies in /usr/local. It confuses ldconfig.

Open questions / next steps:
- Can infra standardize on minimum driver version that supports runtime 12.1? (I think >= 525.x but need confirmation)
- Should we add a node-level probe that checks 'compatibility matrix' (host driver vs container runtime) and labels nodes for scheduling?

Context (symptoms):

- Logs also show: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" and on some runs: "cuDNN library not found: libcudnn.so.8".
- Local dev laptop (NVIDIA 520 driver, CUDA 11.8 toolchain) works fine; CI images use nvidia/cuda:12.1-base by default.

  Result: "Driver Version: 510.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.1" -> mismatch: host driver 510 doesn't fully support runtime 12.1 but nvidia/cuda image reports runtime version 12.1 (container-side toolkit).

    python -c 'import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())'
  Output: |
    2.1.0
    12.1
    True
  Note: torch reports cuda 12.1 but that doesn't guarantee driver compatibility.

- 2025-02-20 14:40 — ldd on libtorch to check linked cuda libs inside the conda env:
  Command: ldd $(python -c "import torch;import os;print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__),'lib','libtorch.so'))") | grep cuda || true
  Observed: some libs linked to /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so -> stub present but actual driver ABI mismatch possible.

- 2025-02-21 09:30 — check host driver package info:
  Commands: cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || dpkg -l | grep nvidia
  Output: "NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  510.54.03  Wed Jul 14 2024"

- 2025-02-22 10:00 — tried reproducer with explicit older CUDA runtime image:
  Command: docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime nvidia-smi && python -c 'import torch;print(torch.version.cuda)'
  Result: driver still 510.x, runtime 11.8, torch prints 11.8 -> fewer compatibility warnings but OOM still sometimes appears.

Concrete error snippets captured from runs:
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 12.34 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 1.00 GiB cached)"
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" (observed in python startup logs once when image was 12.1 but host driver 510)
- "ImportError: libcudnn.so.8: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Host driver is too old for some of the runtime/toolkit combinations used by our images (12.x images) -> occasional ABI issues or silently reduced functionality leading to higher memory usage and OOM.
2) Multiple libcuda.so stubs present (container stubs vs host libcuda) and LD_LIBRARY_PATH picks up wrong one -> symbol mismatches at runtime.
3) cuDNN mismatches: image/conda env expects libcudnn.so.8 but device has a system-installed cuDNN 7.x or nothing -> falls back causing larger workspace allocations or fails to use optimized kernels.
4) Memory leak in our init code (less likely given reproducibility across small tests) combined with driver/runtime mismatch amplifies OOM frequency.

Notes on what matters for compatibility (reminder):
- The NVIDIA driver on the host provides the actual kernel-level support; the CUDA toolkit/runtime in the container can be newer but must be compatible with the host driver (there's a max supported compute/runtime version per driver version).
- libcuda.so (driver API) is provided by host; libcudnn, libcublas etc typically come from the image/env.
- Stubs in /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs are placeholders; if ldd resolves to stubs, the runtime may be routing to host driver at link-time which is OK — but stubs + incompatible host driver => runtime errors.

Title: CUDA library chain debug: heap & driver ABI breadcrumbs

CUDA library chain debug: heap & driver ABI breadcrumbs

Quick scratchpad — trying to capture commands, snippets and hypotheses for a recurring crash we saw on a few Dedicated nodes. Not formal, mostly breadcrumbs for follow-ups.

Problem summary:
- Symptoms: intermittent CUDA OOMs inside containerized PyTorch jobs, often during warmup or eval. Sometimes processes crash with import/runtime errors before any big allocations. Host driver had recently been updated to 535.x.
- Machine: g5.2x (A100-ish equivalent) — single GPU per container.
- Container base: ubuntu:22.04 image built with CUDA runtime libs via apt and conda env for python.

Timeline / attempts:
2025-01-08 09:12 — first repro (local dev node)
- docker run --gpus=all -it --rm --name repro --entrypoint=/bin/bash repro-image
- inside: python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); torch.zeros(1024,1024,1024, device='cuda')"
- error: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 39.00 GiB already allocated)
  - But nvtop/nvidia-smi showed nothing allocated before running script (process list empty).

2025-01-09 11:40 — container import fails in some jobs
- python startup stack: ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
  - ldd $(python -c "import torch; import os, sys; print(torch._C.__file__)" ) shows missing libs pointing to /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0
- However inside container /usr/local/cuda is present; libcudart* are present but symlink versions mismatch (libcudart.so -> libcudart.so.11.8) while torch expects 11.0 SONAME.

Commands used for inspection:
- nvidia-smi
  NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10 Driver Version: 535.86.10 CUDA Version: 12.1
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64 | grep cudart
  lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 20 Jan 1 2024 libcudart.so -> libcudart.so.11.8.74
- ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch._C.__file__)") | grep cudart || true
- ldconfig -p | grep libcudart
- strings /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.8 | head -n 5

Hypothesis A: SONAME mismatch between torch wheel and system CUDA libs
- Some PyTorch builds are linked to a specific SONAME (libcudart.so.11.0) while host has newer 11.x patch with SONAME 11.8 — but usually the SONAME major is 11 so should be compatible. However the import error suggests exact filename missing.
- Quick workaround attempted: create a symlink libcudart.so.11.0 -> libcudart.so.11.8 (temporary) inside container; import succeeds sometimes, but then new errors appear at runtime (segfaults inside cublas).

Hypothesis B: Mixed runtime / driver compatibility (CUDA runtime version vs driver)
- Host driver reports support up to CUDA 12.1, container runtime libs are 11.x — that normally is fine (driver backward compatible). But observed message in some logs: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" when running binary built against 12.x inside container. Possibly one of the model eval tasks is picking up a different libcuda from host path.

Hypothesis C: LD_LIBRARY_PATH / container mount inconsistency leading to partial lib chain (libcudart ok but cuBLAS/cuFFT missing)
- Some containers mount /usr/local/cuda from host as a volume at runtime in our deploys. If the host supplied /usr/local/cuda is from a different driver/toolkit install, it can mismatch.

Interesting logs/tail snippets:
- dmesg | tail after crash:
  [12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, PID=2345, Name: python3, GPU=00000000:01:00.0, Ch 00000040, Class 0x0000b, Reason: Invalid PTX or unsupported relocs
  [12345.679002] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
- kernel logs show TDR-like resets or GPU scheduling errors preceding OOMs for some runs.

Repro attempts and results:
- Create minimal repro that just imports torch and allocates smaller tensors (to isolate warmup): sometimes allocation fails at 16 MiB allocation step with OOM message similar to above.
- Running the same container image on a different host (driver 520.x) did NOT reproduce the segfaults, only the missing-soname import error (fixed with symlink).
- Running with --env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 suppressed some import errors but caused different symbol lookup failures (undefined symbol: cuInit) — indicates mixing of driver lib with different symbol versions.

Commands that changed behavior:
- docker run ... --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:/host-libs:ro ... and then inside container export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-libs:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH 
  -> sometimes fixes import but unstable.
- ldd on /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 shows NEEDED libs to libnvidia-ml.so, etc.

Experiment notes (what I tried, outcome):
- Rebuild image with conda pytorch pinned to cudatoolkit=11.8 instead of expecting system CUDA: reduced import errors, still intermittent OOMs.
- Force embedding allocator to use max_split_size_mb=128 (torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction) — decreased incidence but not eliminated.
- Upgraded driver on one host from 535.x -> 535.99 (minor) — no change.
- Rolled back driver to 520.x on a repro machine — seemed more stable; can't tell if due to driver or different /usr/local/cuda content on that host.

Key hypotheses to test next:
1) Confirm whether /usr/local/cuda is bind-mounted from host in prod deploys (ask infra) — if yes, that explains cross-host variability.
2) Build fully self-contained image that bundles cuda runtime libs (cudatoolkit 11.8 via conda) and ensure no host /usr/local/cuda mounts; run across hosts to see if behavior is consistent.
3) Use nvidia-container-cli to inspect which libs are actually mapped into container at runtime (nvidia-container-cli -k -v list) and snapshot file map for failing run.
4) Reproduce with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and run under gdb to get precise crash backtrace for segfaults.

Quick commands to run for reproducibility capture (add to job wrapper):
- env | grep CUDA
- ldd $(python -c "import torch, sys; print(torch._C.__file__)") || true
- ldconfig -p | grep cuda || true
- nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).xml
- nvidia-container-cli -k -v list --pid $PID > /tmp/nvidia-files.$PID

Notes / reminders:
- Creating naive symlinks can mask the real ABI incompatibility and produce subtle corruption (seen cublas miscomputations).
- Prefer shipping a container with consistent cudatoolkit & torch wheel that match, and avoid mounting host /usr/local/cuda. For Dedicated we sometimes mount host toolkits to save space — that looks risky here.

Raw error excerpts collected:
- "ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.02 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity)"
- dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31"
- python segfault backtrace: "SIGSEGV at 0x7f8c5f000000 in libcudart.so.11.8"

Follow-ups for infra / SRE:
- Confirm whether our deployment templates mount host /usr/local/cuda by default (templates: infra/images/dedicated-runtime.json?)
- Add nvidia-container-cli capture to failing job wrapper to persist file mapping for post-mortem.
- Consider a short pilot to run critical jobs with a fully self-contained image pinned to cudatoolkit=11.8 and no host mounts; compare failure rate for 24h.

If I get time: instrument a tiny C extension that prints cudaDriverGetVersion and cudaRuntimeGetVersion to validate runtime vs driver inside container in the failing environment.

End of notes.

-- Ethan

Title: GPU stack compatibility sleuthing notes

GPU stack compatibility sleuthing notes

Context:
- Intermittent OOMs seen while running a long autoregressive generation (seq_len ~ 8192) on dedicated test node (g5.12xlarge-like). Happens ~30–60m into a continuous load test.
- Suspect: driver/libcuda mismatch, or mixing of system CUDA toolkit + container runtime libs. Also looking at kernel driver updates (node had a driver update during early Feb maintenance window).

Environment snapshot (collected 2025-02-28T09:12):
- kernel: 6.4.17-arch-custom
- nvidia-driver: 535.54.03 (from nvidia-installer)
- CUDA toolkit install: /usr/local/cuda-12.2 (symlinked /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-12.2)
- container base image: ubuntu:22.04 + nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime inside Docker
- container runtime: Docker 24.0 + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.15
- python packages: torch 2.2.0+cu121 wheel built with 12.1, tritonlib 2.0.5, accelerate 0.21

Symptoms (notes):
- Process killed with no Python-level exception; dmesg shows GPU OOM and driver messages.
- Occurs under mixed-precision (amp) in most runs, but reproducible under fp32 if seq_len increased.
- Sometimes the container restarts and subsequent runs succeed for a few hours, then fail again.

Commands tried and outputs (timeline):
1) Basic sanity
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
  -> driver_version: 535.54.03, cuda_version: 12.2
- inside container: python -c "import ctypes, sys; print('libcuda', ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1'))"
  -> loads libcuda from host libs (path resolves), but runtime version mismatch suspected.

2) Check for duplicate libcuda / libcudart
- find /usr -name 'libcuda*.so*' -o -name 'libcudart*.so*' | sed -e 's/^/  /'
  -> multiple entries: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host), /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so.12.2 (toolkit), container image has /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1

3) Run reproducer under strace-like wrapper to capture dlopen paths
- PYTHONVERBOSE=2 python generate_long_sequence.py 2>&1 | tee dlopen.log
  -> observed: dlopen("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1") by libtorch, but later UNABLE to find certain symbol versions in libcudart from container.

4) Attempt LD_PRELOAD trick (temporary test)
- LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so.12.2 python generate_long_sequence.py
  -> short-term improvement: run survived longer (~90m) but still OOMs eventually. Suspect not pure symbol mismatch.

5) Recreate with driver pinned to older version (lab node)
- Rolled back to driver 525.116.04 (matching image used in earlier golden runs)
- After rollback, same workload ran ~8h without OOMs.
  -> Strong indicator driver ABI change introduced instability under heavy KV cache churn.

6) Re-upgrade to 535 and instrumented kernel logs:
- dmesg excerpt (when failure occurred):
  [  605.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, pid=12822, 0 GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [  605.123459] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x36:0x46:124)
  [  605.123461] NVRM: rm init failed, device minor number 0
- Kernel rebind/recovery triggered; container processes killed.

Error snippets captured from worker logs:
- "NCCL WARN TensorPeerAccess: cannot map peer memory"
- Torch CUDA OOM sequence:
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; total 40.00 GiB; free 1.87 GiB)
  Note: free numbers sometimes lie just prior to crash.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver ABI regression (535.x) combined with our long-lived persistent CUDA contexts + aggressive KV cache reuse results in driver-side memory accounting corruption leading to OOMs and device reset. Evidence: rollback to 525 removes issue.
2) Mixed-set of libcudart/libcuda across host and container causing some allocations to be made against different allocators; LD_PRELOAD mitigates slightly but isn't full fix.
3) Kernel module / iommu or PCIe link flakiness causing transient device disconnects under sustained DMA; driver version 535 shows "has fallen off the bus" messages.
4) Application-level leak in kv-cache handling (less likely because same binary + workload on other nodes with 525 is stable).

- Local repro on infra dev box (gcloud vm with A100s) while trying to run model conversion and a smoke serve of a 7B fp16 model.
- Symptoms: intermittent OOMs on both training-style scripts and inference, sometimes accompanied by CUDA runtime/driver errors after package changes.

Commands run (most relevant outputs trimmed):
1) nvidia-smi (host)
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.113.01    Driver Version: 535.113.01    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-SXM4-40GB    Off   | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

2) python checks
$ python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"
2.2.0+cu117 11.7 True

-- mismatch: torch reports CUDA 11.7 support but system driver/runtime is 12.1. This can be OK (newer drivers backward compatible) but we've seen random "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" in other contexts when mixed libs exist.

3) nvcc --version inside container used for conversion
$ nvcc --version
Cuda compilation tools, release 11.7, V11.7.99

4) ldd on libtorch (conda env)
$ python -c "import torch, os; print(torch.__file__)"
.../site-packages/torch
$ ldd .../site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep cudart
	libcudart.so.11.0 => /usr/local/cuda-11.0/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 (0x00007f...)

-- There are multiple libcudart versions on the image; ldconfig shows entries for libcudart.so.11 and libcudart.so.12. The conda torch build is binding to an 11.x ABI but the host has 12.x runtime symlinked in some locations.

5) Docker run check
$ docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.7-runtime-ubuntu20.04 nvidia-smi\(ok)
$ docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi\(ok)

6) Repro command that produced OOM + driver error:
$ python serve.py --model ./7b-fp16 --batch-size 8\Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve.py", line 214, in <module>
    runner = ModelRunner(args)
  File "serve.py", line 98, in __init__
    self.device = torch.device('cuda')
RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid device function
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version

Then later/OOM: "CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.12 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 31.25 GiB already allocated; 1.00 GiB free; 32.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"

Hypotheses so far:
- Mixed libcudart.so versions on PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH (system and container) causing torch to dynamically bind to wrong CUDA runtime at load time.
- PyTorch wheel installed supports CUDA 11.7; driver >= 11.7 should be fine, but if any library (e.g., custom C++ ops, triton, onnxruntime, or libtorch from a different wheel) pulls in a different version ABI it can cause conflicts.
- There are multiple cuda-toolkit packages installed on host (/usr/local/cuda-11.0, /usr/local/cuda-11.7, /usr/local/cuda-12.1) and PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering differs between systemd service, docker runtime, and interactive shells.
- OOMs caused by a memory leak in our conversion step (we do not free CUDA memory between iterations) compounded by fragmentation; fallback after driver error shows inconsistent memory accounting.

What I tried (attempted mitigations):
- Force torch to use the cuda-only wheel matching host: pip install --force-reinstall "torch==2.2.0+cu121" -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html (note: internal policy means some envs still need cu117 build).
- Cleaned LD_LIBRARY_PATH and ensured /usr/local/cuda points to 11.7 during container run: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.7/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
- Added TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to reduce fragmentation: export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
- Used CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 to pin GPUs and run smaller batch sizes (batch 2/4 instead of 8) — reduced OOM frequency but not deterministic.
- Rebuilt custom ops with the system cuda (rebuild triton kernels, custom c++ ops).
- Tried running inside an official nvidia/cuda:11.7 container with matching nvcc and lib paths — that eliminated the driver mismatch errors but OOM still happened in heavy conversion.

Quick notes from logs and stacktraces:
- From /var/log/syslog around time of failure: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" — suggests GPU driver reset after severe failure.
- Python traceback sometimes shows: "Assertion `false && "Illegal memory access"' failed." from CUDA runtime.

Next steps / checklist (for me / infra):
- Reproduce inside a hermetic container with: nvidia/cuda:11.7-runtime + conda env with torch+cu117. If clean, then mismatch is host contamination.
- Run ldconfig -p | grep libcudart to audit multiple installs. If multiple, remove unused symlinks or set container to point to specific library.
- Ask infra to pin driver to a validated version for our AMI family (either 535.x with 12.1 and use cu121 wheels, or install 520.x for 11.7 wheels).
- Add more telemetry: before model load print torch.cuda.memory_summary(), and catch OOM to dump allocation map (torch.cuda.memory_reserved/allocated).
- Add a preflight script to check "python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())'" in the startup and fail fast with a clear message linking to this doc.
- Try enabling "CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1" on a repro run to get a more deterministic backtrace for illegal access.

Notes for escalation email to infra (draft bullet points):
- Observed intermittent: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" while torch reports CUDA 11.7 ABI but nvidia-smi reports CUDA 12.1. There are multiple libcudart versions visible on the host.
- Repro steps included above; consistent elimination of mismatch when running in official 11.7 container, but still hitting OOMs in conversion workloads.
- Request: help standardize AMI to one driver/toolkit pairing (we suggest testing with driver 535 + cu121 wheels, or downgrade system driver to match widely used cu117 internal wheels).
- Request access to the AMI build logs and current ldconfig state for affected machines.

Random helpful links/refs I've used: 
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/12345 (example: "RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version")
- https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/support-matrix/index.html
- Internal infra ticket: INFRA-1423 (GPU driver mismatch investigation)

Unresolved questions / TODOs for me:
- Confirm whether any Python packages in the env ship their own cuda runtime (.so files) — ldd every .so in site-packages that links to cudart.
- Check whether our model conversion step uses CUDA unified memory or calls cuMemAlloc directly.
- Run a small C++ cuda sample that prints runtime vs driver API versions to differentiate which component is complaining.

Short-term workaround for product tests: run conversion in a dedicated job on a pinned AMI/container combination that I verified (11.7 container + cu117 torch wheel) and lower batch sizes.

Longer-term: add an "inference runtime health" check to deployment pipelines that asserts CUDA/driver/torch ABI compatibility and rejects deployments that have mixed runtimes.

Personality notes: this is messy, often noisy — keep incremental notes here. If you copy/paste any outputs into tickets, redact instance ids.

Title: Introduce service-claim circuit breaker and KMS residency prober

Introduce service-claim circuit breaker and KMS residency prober

Adds operator-scoped circuit breaker to prevent unintended cross-region KMS usage, a residency prober for service claims, RBAC v2 policy mapper adjustments, and offline audit collector hardening. Controls are behind feature flags and rollout is canaryed by tenant.
Motivation: Several internal incidents revealed that operator-scoped service claims could accidentally exercise KMS keys in non-resident regions when fallback heuristics engaged. This PR adds a defensive circuit breaker at the service-claim layer that blocks KMS operations when residency constraints fail a liveness/prober check, plus a self-contained residency prober that continuously verifies service-to-region affinity. The change also tightens RBAC v2 mapping so operator-scoped grants are rejected if the claim does not match residency assertions, and hardens the offline audit collector to include provenance tags and scrubbed context for any breaker-triggered events. Implementation overview: 1) New package services/kms/circuit_breaker.go implements a token bucket backed circuit breaker with exponential backoff and a short-term denylist keyed by (service, tenant, attempted_kms_region). The breaker exposes metrics: kms.breaker.allowed, kms.breaker.denied, kms.breaker.backoff_seconds. 2) services/kms/residency_prober.go implements a residency prober that runs a lightweight key-assertion handshake against configured KMS endpoints and caches results with TTL and jitter. Prober results are surfaced to the breaker via a compact status struct. 3) RBAC v2 policy mapping adjusted in rbac/policy/mapper.go to evaluate residency claims (attribute: residency.region) during decision time; missing residency attributes cause a soft-deny path which the breaker can escalate to a hard block when the feature flag is enabled. 4) audit/offline_collector.go extended to include event provenance (prober_result, breaker_reason) and to redact tenant PII for any breaker-related audit forwards. 5) Helm values and operator docs updated to include feature flags rbac.v2.residency_enforce and kms.breaker.enabled and rollout knobs per-tenant. 6) New unit and integration tests covering prober race conditions, breaker backoff behavior, and RBAC attribute evaluation. Migration: tenants with custom KMS mappings must add residency.region claim to service bindings or opt-out by annotation until migration is complete.
Evan Li: Asked for explanation of breaker keying semantics and suggested using tenant-scoped denial histogram; author clarified key is (service, tenant, attempted_region) and added tenant histogram metric; Evan approved after metric added.
Marcus Kim: Noted potential jitter edge-case when prober TTLs align across hosts causing thundering rechecks; requested exponential backoff and randomized jitter; author implemented backoff and updated tests; Marcus requested an additional integration scenario covering network stalls; author added a flakey-tolerant test and Marcus approved.
Sofia Delgado: Security review requested proof that audit redaction removes tenant PII and that provenance tags do not leak keys; author added redaction unit tests and described provenance as summary enums only; Sofia approved with minor doc wording request which was addressed.
QA (Lina Park): Reported intermittent failure in integration test when CI uses mocked KMS with strict timing; added a 50ms tolerance to prober timing in CI and reran; CI passed.
Author (Asha Patel): Responded to all comments and pushed follow-up commits addressing backoff/jitter and audit redaction; requested squash-merge.
Risk: false-positive breaker activations causing client errors. Mitigation: staged rollout with log_only mode and alerting, 48h canary window, quick revert flag kms.breaker.enabled=false.
Risk: increased latency from prober calls. Mitigation: prober uses cached status with TTL and jitter, local cache on each host, and prober calls are async where possible.
Risk: RBAC policy eval path change could affect non-residency tenants. Mitigation: default policy path still allows access unless residency_enforce is turned on; documented opt-out annotation for legacy tenants.
Metrics: kms.breaker.denied, kms.breaker.allowed, kms.breaker.backoff_seconds, rbac.residency_checks.total, audit.breaker_events.count
Dashboards: Security / KMS Residency -> added panel for breaker spikes
Runbook: docs/runbooks/kms-residency-rollout.md contains rollback steps, metrics to watch, and how to disable per-tenant via annotation

Title: P0 Incident Postmortem: Dedicated cluster routing loop causes elevated latency

P0 Incident Postmortem: Dedicated cluster routing loop causes elevated latency

## Summary
On 2026-02-20, one dedicated customer cluster experienced a routing loop between the edge router and the regional policy router after a policy update. This caused request amplification, elevated tail latency, and intermittent 503s for ~19 minutes until policy rollback.

## Severity
P0

## Customer impact
- Impacted: 1 dedicated customer environment in us-west (production).
- Symptoms: p99 latency increased from ~1.2s to > 18s; peak 503 rate 11%.

## Timeline (UTC)
- 05:14: Policy update applied (new fallback rule).
- 05:18: Latency alerts fire; on-call engaged.
- 05:25: Suspected loop; rollback initiated.
- 05:33: Metrics normalize.

## Root cause
A misconfigured fallback route allowed traffic to be re-ingested by the edge router with no loop detection. A recent refactor removed the hop-count header from dedicated routing.

## Detection
Detected via dedicated SLO alerting (latency + 5xx).

## Follow-up action items (count these)
1) Re-introduce hop-count header and enforce max hops (drop with clear error) across dedicated routing. Owning team: Eng Platform.
2) Add loop detection metric and alert (route_reingest_rate > 0.1%). Owning team: Eng SRE.
3) Update dedicated policy editor UI to validate fallback routes for potential self-targeting. Owning team: Eng Platform.
4) Add a dedicated routing integration test that simulates fallback chains and asserts no re-ingest. Owning team: Eng Platform.
5) Document dedicated routing headers (including hop-count) in internal routing spec. Owning team: Eng Platform.

## Lessons learned
- Dedicated routing needs stronger guardrails because misconfigurations have outsized effects.

Title: Tenant stickiness erosion during deferred prewarm leads to cross-variant responses

Tenant stickiness erosion during deferred prewarm leads to cross-variant responses

Issue summary:
BrightForms reported intermittent mixed-model responses for a tenant shortly after a staged model promotion where the system deferred prewarm jobs to prioritize candidate canary capacity. Impact: some requests returned outputs from the legacy model variant instead of the promoted v1 despite the tenant being explicitly pinned to v1.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference returned inconsistent outputs (~4% of requests across a 20-minute window).
- Increased error budgets for the customer's dedicated pool due to retries and fallbacks.
- Customer paused a subset of traffic and escalated to enterprise support.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in prod-us-east served via edge-proxy cluster ep-12.
- Tenant: brightforms-tenant-03 pinned to redwood/caesar-7b-v1.
- Rolling promote executed 2026-03-10T02:15Z with deferred prewarm queue enabled to avoid capacity spike.

Steps to reproduce (from customer repro):
1) Pin tenant to a newly promoted model variant (v1) in dedicated.
2) Trigger staged rollout with deferred prewarm enabled (prewarm tasks scheduled after canary threshold).
3) Send 10k short-chat requests (~15 token prompt) across 10 client connections.
4) Observe ~300 responses that match the legacy model signature (different tokenization/stop sequences).

Observed behavior:
- A subset of requests were routed to the legacy variant within a 12–25s window after promotion.
- Orchestrator logs show tenant affinity assigned to v1, but edge-proxy trace shows a redirect to a node still serving the legacy container.
- KV cache hit metrics for v1 are initially low; legacy variant reports KV hits from cold-requests, implying session routing crossed variants.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant pin should remain honored for all in-flight and new requests after promote commit; deferred prewarm should not allow any routing to legacy once pin committed.

Preliminary investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Deferred prewarm leaves a short window where edge-proxy fallbacks to warm nodes still advertising legacy variant; edge routing uses last-known healthy node when prewarm queue incomplete.
- Hypothesis B: Pin commit is acknowledged by control plane, but the orchestrator's cohort snapshot for a subset of edge shards lags due to snapshot batching; those shards still advertise legacy mapping until snapshot applied.
- Evidence: Orchestrator commit timestamps show commit at 02:15:12Z, but two edge-proxy instances (ep-12-a and ep-12-c) have configuration refresh at 02:15:27Z and 02:15:38Z respectively.
- Additional evidence: We found prewarm-worker logs that deferred container spin-up due to a transient quota error (reserve-gpu failed with EAGAIN) causing warm capacity for v1 to be delayed ~18s.

Immediate impact mitigation applied:
- Support instructed customer to temporarily disable deferred prewarm for the next promotion.
- Control plane team pushed a high-priority config refresh to the affected edge-proxy shard to force snapshot reconciliation.
- SRE increased prewarm-worker retry timeout and added telemetry alert for repeated EAGAIN reserve-gpu.

Next steps (action items):
- SRE to add guard in orchestrator commit path to ensure edge-proxy does not route to legacy variant if pin commit timestamp exists (owner: Ravi, ETA 2026-03-14).
- Runtime team to add a prewarm gating check: if pin committed but prewarm incomplete, queue a soft-block preventing fallback to legacy (owner: Mei Chen, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Add alert that monitors the delta between control-plane commit timestamp and last-edge refresh per shard; trigger when >5s during promotions (owner: Observability, ETA 2026-03-13).
- Postmortem doc to be drafted and linked to Confluence (owner: Support, ETA 2026-03-19).

Attachments/links:
- Edge traces: link to internal trace id trace-ep12-20260310-0216
- Prewarm worker logs: GH-4821 contains extracted logs with EAGAIN timestamps
- Control plane commit log: confluence/rollout-prewarm-sop#commit-20260310

2026-03-10 03:02 - Support (Alicia Moreno): Customer reports mixed outputs; asked for request IDs and example logs. Customer provided 6 request IDs and example payloads.
2026-03-10 04:10 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Pulled orchestrator commit timeline; observed two edge instances lagging by 15-25s. Kicked forced config refresh to ep-12 shard. Noted prewarm worker errors in GH-4821.
2026-03-10 05:01 - Customer (BrightForms Ops): Confirmed that after disabling deferred prewarm for subsequent promotion, they saw no mixed responses in a follow-up run of 20k requests.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Runtime (Mei Chen): Adding proposal for prewarm gating; will implement a soft block that prevents routing to legacy variant if pin committed but prewarm incomplete. Draft PR GH-4830 opened.
2026-03-12 16:45 - Support (Alicia Moreno): Drafted customer communication summarizing workaround and next steps; scheduled follow-up call for 2026-03-13 10:00 UTC.
Workaround: disable deferred prewarm for sensitive promotions; manual config refresh applied. Long-term fix planned (gating and edge commit checks).

Title: Enforced model pin suppressed by fallback-throttle preemption during canary window, causing mixed-model responses

Enforced model pin suppressed by fallback-throttle preemption during canary window, causing mixed-model responses

Issue summary: Customer BrightAssist reported intermittent mixed-model outputs despite having an explicit tenant model pin configured. Impact: a subset (~4%) of requests during the canary window returned responses generated by a compat/legacy variant instead of the pinned model, causing degraded answer quality and downstream QA alerts. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod(us-east), pinned via tenant config to redwood-7b-v1.
1) Tenant has explicit pin: tenant_config.pin_model = 'redwood-7b-v1'
2) Trigger canary rollout for redwood-7b-v1 -> redwood-7b-v2 in same region with 10% weight
3) Simulate load spike with concurrent prefix-heavy streams (50 RPS sustained for 10m)
4) Observe router logs and serving runtime traces for requests that should honor tenant pin
edge-proxy trace: req=1a7c3f7e tenant=brightassist route=chat model_hint=redwood-7b-v1 fallback_reason=throttle_preemptor selected_model=redwood-1.5b-v2
orchestrator log snippet: 2026-03-11T15:42:08Z WARN fallback-controller: preemptive-throttle triggered for slice 10; suppressed explicit_pin=true for cohort 'tenant-42' to preserve SLOs
serving-runtime: request_id=1a7c3f7e latency=1200ms kvcache_hits=0 selected_variant=compat-v1 (fallback path)
2026-03-11 16:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer reported unexpected answer changes at ~15:40 UTC during canary. Provided request IDs and example outputs. They see mixed outputs for some user sessions despite explicit pin.
2026-03-11 16:22 - SRE (Liam Chen): Reproduced similar trace in prod; fallback-controller emitted preemptive-throttle event and set decision to allow degraded variant for a short window. Investigating why explicit pin was not honored.
2026-03-11 17:04 - Eng (Priya Sundar): Hypothesis: fallback-controller has a higher priority rule for latency mitigation that can preempt per-tenant pins when aggregate slot pressure exceeds a threshold. Need to confirm the rule evaluation order and recent config changes.
2026-03-11 19:30 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (rollback canary and set strict capacity cap). Asking for ETA on fix and whether billing will be adjusted for impacted requests.
2026-03-12 09:18 - Eng (Liam Chen): Identified change in controller ordering deployed 2026-03-10 (PR #872) that introduced 'preemptive-throttle' as a higher-priority branch. Preparing a rollback of that behavioral change for emergency patch.
2026-03-14 11:10 - Eng (Liam Chen): Hotfix deployed to route-controller that enforces tenant pin precedence over preemptive fallback except under Sev0 global overload. Monitoring telemetry; customer confirmed no mixed-model responses in last 6 hours. Drafting follow-up change to add metrics and a toggle.
2026-03-14 11:45 - Customer (BrightAssist - T. Moreno): Confirmed improved behavior and restored quality. Asked for postmortem and timeline for full fix.
Initial triage: Not an auth or cookie issue. All affected requests had valid pin metadata attached at the ingress layer.
Correlated events: A canary rollout in the same region created a transient slot pressure pattern; fallback-controller responded by enabling preemptive-throttle to maintain P95 latency SLOs across tenants.
Root cause hypothesis: Route-controller policy evaluation order was changed in PR #872; preemptive-throttle branch was assigned a precedence above explicit tenant pin checks, allowing it to override pins during short overload windows.
Telemetry: During the incident window (15:38 - 15:51 UTC) fallback-controller logged 1,340 preemptive events; of those ~52 had explicit_pin=true and were forced to compat-variant selection.
Partial repro: Replayed the same traffic profile against staging with the new policy and reproduced pin suppression consistently when queue depth > 800 and prewarm cache miss ratio > 60%.
Edge-case note: Requests that were streaming with prefix > 1024 tokens disproportionately hit the fallback path due to increased per-token cost estimation and conservative slot accounting in the throttle algorithm.
Immediate mitigation (2026-03-11 20:10 UTC): Rolled back policy precedence change from PR #872 in the route-controller and toggled off preemptive-throttle for non-global overload conditions. Customer canary rolled back at their request to stop quality variance.
Hotfix (2026-03-14 11:05 UTC): Deployed patch that enforces explicit tenant pin precedence in policy evaluator. Added safety check to allow preemptive-throttle only when global cluster overload is detected (Sev0).
Follow-ups / action items:
- ENG-8471: Add telemetry and dashboards for 'pin-suppressed-by-fallback' events (owner: Priya Sundar).
- OPS-5490: Add a canary guard that isolates pinned-tenants from preemptive-throttle decisions unless explicitly opted-in (owner: Liam Chen).
- CS to offer credit: recommend finance review for impacted token billing with BrightAssist (owner: Maya Patel).
- Postmortem: Schedule postmortem and publish to Confluence with timeline and corrective steps (owner: SRE lead).
Customer status: BrightAssist confirmed behavior stable as of 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC; team requested formal postmortem and follow-up on billing impact.
